# Changelog

## Unreleased

- Fixed shared page headers squeezing Updates and other stacked-content pages into narrow flex columns. Catalog, Systems and Research now explicitly opt into horizontal header rows, which stack at widths of 800px and below.

## 2.0.0 — 2026-10-16

- Migrated all 52 records and 9 notes to normalized source, claim, build, mechanism, validation, relationship, correction and dossier contracts. Version 2 exports replace the obsolete version 1 endpoints and embedded evidence fields.
- Preserved the function-level EAC dispute without treating either the critique's existence or a newer upstream commit as proof of whole-program correctness. Original and later measurements, mirror access and independent-validation limits remain distinct.
- Added consistent eight-aspect dossiers for nine systems and ten-topic mechanism worksheets, with specific unanswered questions instead of guessed internals.
- Replaced the promotional landing page with a compact, search-first table and Catalog / Systems / Research / Updates navigation. Results expose claim states, build scope and review dates; mobile filters/outlines collapse and tables scroll locally.
- Added build-generated Pagefind search for system, driver, hash, CVE, mechanism, function and source text. Supported main-thread WASM mode avoids the observed worker URL failure; result URLs respect the application's canonical paths and GitHub Pages prefixes.
- Added a durable discovery inbox, canonical/origin grouping, approved publisher archive and repository-history backfill, public release/issue metadata, bounded source/version diffs, re-review links, daily collection and weekly digests. Initial fingerprints are baselines, not invented publication edits; inaccessible sources retain earlier discoveries.
- Added local bookmarks, saved queries, entity/source watches and validated JSON backup/restore, plus update and digest RSS with revision-specific GUIDs.
- Added build-scoped comparisons, sourced relationship graphs with table alternatives, and a reproducibility ledger/proposal workspace. Author-reported execution stays distinct from Observatory observation.
- Added schema-checked browser proposal downloads and transactional CLI imports, stale-output invalidation, evidence/collection regressions in CI, and explicit MIT code / CC BY 4.0 original-content licensing.
- Excluded researcher profiles, author directories and taxonomy/index pages from new discovery and legacy snapshots; retained-publication triage and digest references remain consistent.
- Mechanism topics share a deduplicated evidence section, preserving a single stable anchor per claim instead of repeating citation blocks across worksheet cells.

- Upgraded Astro from 5.x to 7.4.0 to resolve dependency advisories; declared Node.js 22.22.0 as the minimum supported runtime and refreshed the lockfile.
- Fixed scheduled refresh deployment: the default-branch sync job explicitly dispatches the Pages workflow after its bot commit, with scoped Actions write permission. `GITHUB_TOKEN` pushes do not trigger push workflows.
- Fixed GitHub Pages route collisions when a repository base matches an application route, such as `/blog/`.
- Project detail pages now highlight Projects in the main navigation.
- Editing a prepared publishing draft now revokes its old download and clears the previous output and GitHub shortcut; failed validation cannot leave a stale publishable result visible.
- Removed the obsolete researcher-social branch from the publishing logic and corrected documentation that incorrectly promised a missing-feed fallback.
- Reverified production builds, dependency audit, rendered pages and internal links, mobile layouts, browser downloads, publishing state transitions, live source retrieval and the workflow's local commit/push behavior.
- Corrected the EAC Linux project entry after an external correctness critique: its summary now identifies partial, disputed AI-assisted recovery, the critique and retrieval limits are cited, and the former endorsement has been withdrawn.
- Pinned EAC measurements to README revision `10d67114e3` (including 1,313 patched branches and 27 tests), with later `dc5f947d75` author-reported results explicitly separate and no implied resolution of the dispute.
- Added `Community report` to catalog section labels with mandatory attribution, and made existing section evidence labels visible on record and blog pages using the established styles. Specific public-post citations are allowed without restoring personal-profile links.
- Added `RESEARCH-ROADMAP.md`: scoped claims, version/sample identity, contradictions, a durable discovery inbox, deep-dossier requirements, feature priorities and a simpler search-first UI.

## 1.2.0 — 2026-10-16

Link policy

- Removed every researcher social profile, personal handle and tweet link from the source directory, records and notes, and dropped the `Researcher social` source type from the schema so it cannot be reintroduced by the publishing form. Attribution now comes from publisher bylines and repository URLs.

Deep-dive research projects

- Added a `project` record kind with `repoUrl`, `repoLicense`, `repoLanguage` and `reviewedCommit`, plus a `/projects` showcase, project cards, and a repository panel on each project page.
- Added four project records: `eac-linux-devirt` (EAC Linux `plx.elf` devirtualization), `ironshield-analysis` (`tvk.sys` static analysis), `ring-one-io` (UEFI bootloader implant deobfuscation) and `chernobog` (Hikari LLVM obfuscation recovery tooling).
- Products and projects now cross-link: product pages list the deep dives that examine them, and project pages list the records they analyze.

New system and coverage

- Added the Ironshield system dossier, the `tvk.sys` kernel driver record, and a finding for the reported IOCTL authorization weaknesses — including the certificate substring check, statically derivable LEA key, client-supplied symbol offsets, and the reachable IOCTL capabilities, all attributed to the published analysis with its unresolved remediation status.
- Added ten technique studies: IOCTL authorization, handle access filtering, image load filtering, driver client authentication, kernel symbol resolution, driver transport encryption, protected process light, runtime driver attestation, Linux/Proton anti-cheat, and enforcement/privacy/appeals.
- Added `/coverage`: a per-system map across components, techniques, findings, projects and notes that shows explicit gaps and the cross-vendor queue.

Automated source feed

- Added `npm run sync`, which fetches RSS/Atom research feeds and GitHub repository state into `src/data/feed.json`, recording blocked sources with their HTTP status instead of omitting them, and preserving previous repository snapshots as stale when a fetch fails.
- Added upstream drift detection: each project record pins a `reviewedCommit`, and the site flags when a repository head moves past it, including on the project card, project page and `/feed`.
- Added `/feed` with source status cards, the latest publications, the tracked-repository table, and documentation of the workflow; added `/api/v1/feed.json`.
- Added the weekly `sync-sources.yml` workflow, which refreshes the snapshot with a repository token, validates it, commits when changed, and emits `::warning::` annotations for upstream drift.
- Extended validation to project repository fields and the feed snapshot, including that every tracked repository agrees with its record's `reviewedCommit`.

`README.md`:

```md
# Anti-Cheat Observatory

A version-scoped, source-backed reference to anti-cheat systems and the public research about them. The unit of knowledge is not an article or a repository — it is a **scoped, attributable claim** with an explicit evidence origin, review activity, claim state and applicability.

Astro + TypeScript, static output, Git-backed JSON content, GitHub Pages hosting. No backend, database, account or external contributor workflow is required.

## The problem this model exists to solve

An artifact can simultaneously be valuable, partially correct, externally disputed, and not independently reproduced. A single "verified" badge cannot express that, and a function-level criticism must not be allowed to either condemn or vindicate an entire body of research.

So the catalog separates three axes that are usually collapsed:

| Axis | Values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **Provenance** | vendor, publication, repository, community, academic, disclosure, unverified | Who supplied the assertion |
| **Review activity** | collected, source-inspected, artifact-inspected, behavior-reproduced | What the Observatory actually did |
| **Claim state** | asserted, corroborated, disputed, refuted, superseded | Where the assertion currently stands |

Structural guards require distinct declared origin IDs for `corroborated`, an explicit challenge for `disputed`, attributed counterevidence for `refuted`, and a replacement claim for `superseded`. The maintainer must still establish source independence and judge the evidence: mirrors, reposts and revisions of one work share an origin.

`artifact-inspected` requires an authorized, dated, observed inspection record. `behavior-reproduced` additionally requires a passing execution record for a hashed build within the claim's scope; it cannot borrow a sample identity from another validation. These checks establish consistency, not binary correctness.

## Quick start

Node.js 22.22.0 or newer (required by Astro 7).

```sh
npm install
npm run dev        # local preview with hot reload
npm run check      # Astro/TypeScript diagnostics
npm run validate   # schema, cross-reference, dispute and discovery integrity
npm test           # deterministic evidence, importer and discovery regressions
npm run build      # validate, build the static site, then generate the Pagefind index
npm run preview    # serve the built dist/
npm run sync       # collect public source metadata (network; see Maintenance)
npm run digest     # regenerate the weekly discovery digest
npm run import -- proposal.json [--replace] [--dry-run]
npm run format     # Prettier for source, content, and config
```

Astro picks a free port if the default is busy; pass `-- --port 4341` to request one.

## Site map

Primary destinations: **Catalog · Systems · Research · Updates**. Everything else is secondary.

| Route | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `/` and `/catalog` | Search-first catalog: kind, vendor, platform, layer, period and claim-state filters, plus static full-text search |
| `/systems` | The nine system dossiers and their completeness |
| `/research` | Research projects and tooling, filtered from the catalog |
| `/updates` | Corrections, disputes, editorial revisions, and the pending source-change queue |
| `/records/<id>` | A record: scoped claims, cited sources, builds, mechanisms, corrections |
| `/claims/<id>` | One claim: statement, applicability, evidence locators, contradictions, validations |
| `/sources/<id>` | One source: revision identity, access, transport, mirror origin, rights, dependent claims |
| `/builds/<id>` | One sample/build: reported versus computed hashes, scope, limitations |
| `/mechanisms/<id>` | Technical worksheet: trigger, context, conditions, primitives, counterexamples, unknowns |
| `/coverage` | Per-system evidence across the eight dossier aspects, with explicit gaps; dossiers live at `/records/<system-id>` |
| `/relationships` | Evidence-backed relationship explorer with a table alternative |
| `/compare` | Version-scoped comparison of documented mechanisms (never a strength ranking) |
| `/workspace` | Authorized reproducibility ledger and validation-proposal builder |
| `/library` | Local bookmarks, watches and saved queries (browser storage only) |
| `/projects`, `/blog`, `/blog/<id>` | Project showcase, editorial notes, and one note |
| `/feed` | Unreviewed discovery: publisher metadata, retrieval status, backfill scope |
| `/matrix`, `/methodology`, `/data`, `/publishing` | Trust-boundary reading map, evidence contract, dataset documentation, publishing workspace |
| `/api/v2/*`, `/updates.xml`, `/digest.xml` | Machine-readable exports and feeds |

## Evidence model

Files live in `src/data/knowledge/` (collections plus `validations/<id>.json`) and `src/data/records/`, `src/data/posts/`. The contract is `src/data/knowledge.schema.json`; types are `src/lib/knowledge-types.ts`; query helpers are `src/lib/knowledge.ts`.

| Entity | Purpose |
|---|---|
| System / integration | Vendor, product, platform, lifecycle, documented boundaries — a product family is not one immutable deployment |
| Component | Driver, service, library, launcher or server boundary with documented responsibilities |
| Mechanism | Canonical behavior or interface with build-specific claims and a full technical worksheet |
| Sample / build | Filename, version, source-reported versus project-computed hash, provenance, scope |
| Source / revision | Original URL, immutable revision identity, access state, transport, origin, rights, limitations |
| Claim | One assertion with scope, locators, supporting and contradicting evidence, limitations, state |
| Finding | Root cause and disclosure history — a weakness is not automatically a current bypass |
| Investigation / project | Question, tools, input identity, reported validation, unresolved functions, criticisms |
| Correction / event | What changed, which claim or revision it affects, and its resolution status |

Records keep stable IDs and stable URLs. A record's `sections` reference claim IDs; claims reference sources, builds and mechanisms. `relatedIds` is editorial browsing metadata and is explicitly **not** evidence of an architectural or implementation relationship — those live in `relationships.json`, where every edge must cite a claim that itself has citations.

### The EAC dispute as the reference case

`eac-linux-devirt` is the catalog's worked example of not collapsing distinct claims. The reviewed revision (`10d67114e3`) and a later upstream revision (`dc5f947d75`) carry separately scoped author-reported measurements; the function-level correctness question for `0x237F0` is an open dispute in which the critique and the recovery remain linked but not resolved; `correction-eac-237f0` records before/after wording. A newer commit cannot silently close the dispute, because resolution requires evidence addressing the specific criticism.

The catalog has not reproduced that devirtualization or validated either comparison against the original binary, and no claim here asserts a current bypass.

## Maintenance

The build consumes committed research data and does not run source collection. Dependency installation needs normal package access; collection is a separate command that writes the snapshot.

```sh
npm run sync                      # poll sources whose interval has elapsed
npm run sync -- --force           # poll every configured source
npm run sync -- --backfill        # inspect only the configured bounded historical endpoints
npm run digest                    # regenerate the weekly digest
```

`src/data/discovery-sources.json` is the reviewed source registry: approved HTTPS endpoints, acquisition kind, scope, interval, and bounded backfill endpoints. `src/data/discovery.json` is the durable snapshot; `src/data/discovery-state.json` holds content fingerprints used for change detection.

What it does:

- **RSS/Atom** — approved feeds have an 8 MB transport cap, with at most 100 entries processed per poll and 350-character summaries retained. Full article bodies embedded in a feed are not republished. Known tracking parameters are removed without collapsing meaningful URL variants.
- **GitHub** — head and reviewed revisions, up to 30 public releases and 30 recently updated public issues per poll, and bounded commit comparison patches. Pull requests and draft releases are excluded; an issue remains an unreviewed report.
- **Documents/pages** — bounded public text metadata; PDFs are version-probed by HTTP header only and are never downloaded or executed.
- **Historical backfill** — up to three pages of 100 public commits per configured repository; approved sitemaps and dated HTML article indexes are bounded to eight requests and 300 URLs. HTML indexes contribute article links, titles and index-reported dates, not author profiles or article bodies. Their coverage remains partial. Sitemap-derived labels never overwrite an inspected feed title.
- **Change detection** — bounded feed metadata, page titles/descriptions/headings, document version headers and repository patches. The first publication fingerprint establishes a baseline; enriching or normalizing an older snapshot is not evidence of an upstream edit. This is not a full-body archive or a semantic correctness check.
- **Publication eligibility** — known researcher-profile, author-directory and tag/category/index URL patterns are excluded from discovery and pruned from older snapshots. Passing this filter makes a URL a candidate, not a reviewed research finding.

What it refuses to do:

- A blocked forum stays an inaccessible lead. Titles are not converted into bodies, and access controls are not bypassed.
- Never-attempted sources are `pending`, not `error`; a blocked source keeps its last success, retained items and honest status.
- Discovered items are **unreviewed metadata**. They never advance a `reviewedCommit` and never change a claim state.
- Mirrors are recorded as mirrors. Two mirrors of one document are one origin, not corroboration.
- Historical coverage is recorded as inspected ranges. A latest-items feed is not an archive, and the snapshot says so.

`.github/workflows/sync-sources.yml` runs daily, generates the digest on the weekly schedule, validates, commits only discovery files when they changed, and then explicitly dispatches `pages.yml` — a push made with `GITHUB_TOKEN` does **not** trigger another push workflow. It needs `contents: write` to commit and `actions: write` to dispatch, and repository rules must permit the bot to update the default branch. No personal access token is required.

To expand collection, add an approved endpoint and its explicit scope to the registry, then run `npm run sync -- --backfill`. Do not add arbitrary article traversal. Inspect the inbox before drafting sources/claims through `/publishing`; import the proposal as described below. In `src/data/discovery.json`, manually set an item's `review` to `linked` or `dismissed` after triage, and a source change's `review` to `reviewed` only after inspecting the relevant evidence. Collection preserves those decisions and never advances a project's reviewed commit.

## Updating the reference

Browser drafting, followed by a local import:

1. Open `/publishing` (or `/workspace` for a validation record) and fill in the source, scoped claims and note.
2. The page validates against the full schema and runs the same semantic and cross-reference guards as the CLI, then downloads a `KnowledgeProposal`.
3. Import it with `npm run import -- <proposal.json>`; use `--dry-run` first, or `--replace` to revise an existing ID.
4. Inspect the diff, run `npm run build`, exercise the affected pages, then commit to the default branch. GitHub Actions validates and publishes.

If you deliberately change a project's reviewed commit, run `npm run sync` before building so the repository snapshot re-derives that pin from the record. This does not establish correctness or advance any claim's review state; the associated source/build evidence still needs its own inspection.

The importer is transactional: it validates the proposal, then the merged catalog, then stages every file and re-checks that the catalog did not change underneath it before replacing anything — rolling back if it did. It never auto-promotes a claim state or silently links a validation.

Editorial rules before committing:

1. Establish the product, component, version, provenance and the question being answered.
2. Inspect the original publication when reachable. If a permitted mirror is the only transport, record it and exactly which material was available; a snippet or generated summary is not inspected source text.
3. Attach evidence to the specific claim it supports, with a real locator, and leave unknowns explicit.
4. Never convert a historical finding into a current exposure, or a vulnerability into an anti-cheat bypass.
5. Never mark behavior reproduced without an authorized, bounded execution record with a hashed sample.
6. Run `npm run build`, then exercise the changed pages.

## Deploying on GitHub Pages

`.github/workflows/pages.yml` validates on every pull request and push, then builds and deploys only from the default branch (`workflow_dispatch` also deploys manually).

This checkout is already an initialised Git repository (`main`, one commit). Create the remote and push:

```sh
# With the GitHub CLI, this creates the repository and pushes in one step:
gh repo create anti-cheat-observatory --public --source=. --remote=origin --push

# Without the CLI, create an empty repository in the GitHub UI, then:
git remote add origin git@github.com:<owner>/anti-cheat-observatory.git
git push -u origin main
```

Then:

1. Repository → Settings → Pages → Source: **GitHub Actions**.
2. Push to the default branch or run the workflow manually.

Set the `PUBLIC_REPOSITORY` variable to `<owner>/anti-cheat-observatory` so edit links resolve.

The workflow runs `actions/configure-pages` and passes its origin and base path into the build, so the same code serves a user site at `/`, a project site at `/repo/`, and a custom domain. Optional repository variables override them:

| Variable | Effect |
|---|---|
| `SITE_URL` | Absolute site origin, e.g. `https://observatory.example` (also used for absolute RSS links) |
| `BASE_PATH` | Root-relative base, e.g. `/anti-cheat-observatory/` |
| `PUBLIC_REPOSITORY` | `owner/repo`, enables edit links and the footer GitHub link |
| `PUBLIC_REPOSITORY_BRANCH` | Branch used by edit links; defaults to `main` |

Locally:

```sh
SITE_URL=https://example.github.io BASE_PATH=/anti-cheat-observatory/ \
  PUBLIC_REPOSITORY=example/anti-cheat-observatory npm run build
```

Internal routes, assets, downloads, fetches and form actions use `withBase()` in `src/lib/paths.ts`. Search uses Pagefind's supported main-thread WASM mode because its relative metadata fetches failed in the observed blob-worker context; this avoids a worker URL workaround at the cost of running queries on the UI thread. Indexed result links follow the site's no-trailing-slash routes. Configure `SITE_URL` for absolute published RSS links; local builds without it retain relative links instead of guessing an origin.

## Publication and rights

- No proprietary driver samples, cheat payloads, live "undetected" feeds, credentials, private telemetry, or undisclosed vulnerability details belong in this repository.
- A vulnerable driver is not automatically malicious, and is not automatically an anti-cheat bypass. A successful driver load, API import, crash, or ban-free period does not prove evasion.
- A purported leak may have a metadata record stating its authenticity, public source and uncertainty. Public availability does not authorize mirroring stolen source, proprietary dumps, personal data, or undisclosed vulnerabilities.
- Do not turn a research reference into a live bypass service.

### Licenses

- **Application code, templates, schemas and configuration**: [MIT](LICENSE).
- **Original editorial prose and curated catalog data** (`src/data/records/`, `posts/`, `knowledge/`, and original in-page prose): [CC BY 4.0](LICENSE-CONTENT).
- **Third-party material** — linked publications, repositories, screenshots, binaries and quoted material — retains its own rights and is cited, not relicensed. Third-party excerpts stay minimal and attributed.

Both licenses are conventional defaults chosen so the project can be reused and cited; change them before publishing if you want different terms. `RESEARCH-ROADMAP.md` documents the model's design; this README documents what is implemented.

The secret.club dated index supplied 55 article links spanning 2019-01-09 through 2026-05-21; these remain unreviewed metadata, not inspected article bodies. Known profile/index links are excluded, and unavailable sources retain their status and earlier data.

Use `npm run build` followed by `npm run preview` to exercise Pagefind; `npm run dev` does not generate the static search index. These checks verify the application's behavior, not anti-cheat binary semantics or independent research reproduction. GitHub deployment was not executed locally.

`RESEARCH-ROADMAP.md`:

```md
# Research catalog roadmap

Status: implemented in 2.0.0. This document preserves the accepted design; see `README.md` for operation and exercised verification. Research coverage remains selected and version-scoped, with explicit gaps—not an exhaustive inventory or a claim of independent binary reproduction.

## Direction

Build a versioned anti-cheat research reference, not a collection of bypass headlines or a general security-news feed. Keep GitHub Pages, static output, Git-backed structured content and a single-maintainer workflow. The blog explains investigations; it is not the underlying database.

The unit of knowledge should be a **scoped, attributable claim**. A repository, paper or forum thread is a source, not a truth verdict. The EAC Linux correction demonstrates why: an artifact can be valuable, partially recovered, externally disputed and not independently reproduced at the same time.

"Every weakness, leak and reversed detail" is a discovery ambition, not a completeness claim. Closed server internals, inaccessible threads, unpublished work and unknown builds cannot honestly be cataloged as known facts. Publish the coverage boundary and missing evidence instead.

## 1. Knowledge model

Evolve the existing records without maintaining a second parallel catalog. Migrate existing citations and relationships into these entities, retain stable page URLs, and version exported contracts when their shape changes.

| Entity | Required information | Why it exists |
|---|---|---|
| System / integration | Vendor, product, game integration, platform, lifecycle, documented boundaries | A product family is not one immutable deployment |
| Component | Driver, service, library, launcher, server boundary or firmware component; documented responsibilities | Do not assign every behavior to a kernel driver |
| Mechanism | Canonical behavior or interface, with build-specific claims and linked implementation evidence | Keep a general technique distinct from a claim that a vendor actually implements it |
| Sample / build | Filename, platform, version, source-reported hash, independently computed hash if available, provenance, acquisition date and source | A filename, certificate or version string alone is not identity |
| Source / revision | Original URL, publication and access dates, author attribution without profile links, repository commit or permitted snapshot digest, access status and rights | Claims must remain interpretable when the upstream page changes |
| Claim | One assertion, component/build scope, exact source locator, observation versus inference, supporting and contradicting sources, limits, review activity and claim state | Contradictions must attach to the specific assertion, not disappear inside an article |
| Finding | Root cause, trust boundary, prerequisites, reported impact, affected/fixed build evidence, CVE/advisory links and disclosure history | A weakness must not automatically become a current bypass claim |
| Investigation / project | Question, tools and versions, input identity, recovered artifacts, reported validation contract, unresolved functions, independent checks and criticisms | Function counts and screenshots do not prove whole-program equivalence |
| Correction / event | What changed, which claim/revision it affects, reason, evidence, date and resolution status | Corrections and superseded claims remain discoverable |

### Separate three axes

- **Provenance:** vendor documentation, research publication, source repository, community report, public disclosure or unverified provenance.
- **Review activity:** collected, source inspected, artifact inspected, behavior reproduced. Reproduction must identify who performed it and its bounded contract.
- **Claim state:** asserted, corroborated, disputed, refuted or superseded. Missing version applicability remains explicitly unknown.

Do not use a single green badge, star count or numeric confidence score to collapse these axes. "Source reviewed" is not "verified correct". One source mirrored on several sites is still one source.

### Minimum claim contract

Every technical assertion needs a stable ID, plain-language assertion, linked system/component, applicable platform/build or explicit unknown scope, original source/revision, a source locator (section, function RVA, source line or timestamp), evidence description, limitations, review date, supporting/contradicting relationships and a claim state. Address-bearing observations must identify the address space and image base when relevant. Preserve the distinction between a source-reported hash and a hash computed by this project.

## 2. Depth required for each system

Use one consistent dossier outline. Each cell is documented, partially documented or unknown, with evidence links; a missing cell is not evidence that a feature is absent.

1. **Deployment and lifecycle:** launcher, installation, boot/game/session start, update delivery, shutdown, game-specific settings and supported platforms.
2. **Component inventory:** drivers, services, libraries and remote boundaries; filenames, signers, versions, hashes and provenance where lawfully available.
3. **Interfaces and trust boundaries:** device objects, documented IOCTL or IPC responsibilities, caller authorization, client/server authority and boundary assumptions.
4. **Observed mechanisms:** process/handle callbacks, image loading, integrity checks, telemetry, enforcement, boot trust, attestation and virtualization-related observations. Separate vendor descriptions from sample-specific recovered behavior.
5. **Code protection and recovery:** protector attribution, VM/function inventory, recovered versus unresolved paths, toolchain, compiler effects and validation scope. A devirtualized count is not a correctness percentage.
6. **Publicly disclosed weaknesses and incidents:** mechanism/root cause, environment and prerequisite scope, impact, mitigation evidence, affected/fixed versions and open disputes. No unsupported "works today" labels.
7. **Research trail:** papers, repositories, forum claims, public status posts, corrections and provenance relationships. Specific posts may be cited; personal profile directories remain out of scope.
8. **History and gaps:** versioned changes, stale claims, unresolved questions, inaccessible sources and work needed to fill each gap.

For every mechanism, use a technical worksheet: trigger and lifecycle, execution context, inputs and outputs, inspected decision conditions, protected object, documented OS primitives versus custom logic, dependencies and trust assumptions, evidence/function locators, tested cases, counterexamples and unknowns. Track callbacks, IPC, memory operations, integrity checks and telemetry at this granularity rather than writing one generic paragraph about a driver. Use CWE or other established taxonomies only where a supported mapping exists.

EAC and Ironshield are the primary deep-dive pilots. The same dossier and worksheet contracts now cover BattlEye, Vanguard, FACEIT, RICOCHET, Javelin and ACE. Per-system questions expose the remaining evidence backlog; a filled outline does not establish complete research.

## 3. Discovery and maintenance pipeline

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Sources[Approved public sources] --> Collect[Collect metadata and permitted excerpts]
  Collect --> Normalize[Canonicalize and deduplicate]
  Normalize --> Inbox[Unreviewed research inbox]
  Inbox --> Inspect[Inspect originals and pin revisions]
  Inspect --> Claims[Create or revise scoped claims]
  Claims --> Validate[Validate data and exercise affected pages]
  Validate --> Publish[Commit and publish static site]
  Sources --> Changes[Detect edits, corrections and new commits]
  Changes --> Inbox
```

### Collect broadly; promote narrowly

- Maintain a source registry with acquisition method, product/topic scope, access status, polling policy and canonical URL. Track publishers, selected repository releases/commits/issues, vendor advisories and relevant public forum threads.
- Preserve discovered items in a durable registry. The former ten-items-per-feed snapshot has been replaced; later polling must not erase older discoveries or manual triage decisions.
- Canonicalize tracking URLs; connect mirrors, reposts and forks to the original. Keep source independence separate from URL count. Rank anti-cheat-specific items above unrelated publisher posts.
- A blocked forum remains an inaccessible lead. Do not manufacture a summary from its title, silently drop failures or bypass access controls. Authorized manual imports can provide reviewed text later.
- Prefer publisher RSS/Atom and official GitHub/vendor endpoints. Social-post acquisition needs an authorized API, a permitted public retrieval or an imported specific-post URL; unofficial mirrors are fallible transports, not guaranteed complete archives. Preserve which transport was used and never treat two mirrors as independent testimony.
- Backfill permitted publisher archives, sitemaps, category indexes, repository histories and already-known public disclosures before relying on incremental feeds. Track which source/date ranges were inspected and which remain unreviewed; a latest-items feed cannot stand in for a deep historical catalog.
- Separate the public, explicitly unreviewed discovery feed from the reviewed catalog. New feed items and repository commits do not automatically change claim states, reviewed commits or remediation conclusions.
- AI may propose tags, relationships, summaries and contradiction candidates, but every factual sentence needs an inspected source locator. It must not certify its own reverse engineering or turn tests it generated into independent corroboration.
- Run daily metadata discovery and a weekly focused maintenance digest, bounded by each source's approved scope and polling interval.
- Keep collection in GitHub Actions. Fetch data only: never execute newly discovered repository code, forum attachments or driver samples in a token-bearing publishing job. Any model credentials belong in Actions secrets, never browser JavaScript.

### One-maintainer operating loop

1. Open the generated inbox, prioritized by corrections, disputes, vendor fixes, upstream drift and then new research.
2. Inspect original material; update a claim rather than creating a duplicate article for every repost.
3. Review the proposed source/claim diff, including removed evidence and altered version applicability.
4. Run structural checks and smoke the affected dossier, search result and exports.
5. Commit once; Actions deploys. Keep a weekly summary of what was added, corrected, superseded or still blocked.

No additional contributor is required. Scheduled retrieval can run unattended; deep analysis requires an assistant run or separately configured analysis workflow. A static site does not perform new independent research by itself.

## 4. Feature priorities and acceptance

| Priority | Deliverable | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| P0 | Atomic claims, immutable source revisions and contradiction links | One function-level criticism can be linked without labeling unrelated results false; original and later revisions remain distinguishable |
| P0 | Build/sample identities and applicability | A historical finding cannot be presented as affecting an unexamined current build; reported and computed hashes are distinguishable |
| P0 | Corrections and validation ledger | Every "reproduced" statement identifies an execution record and contract; a repair commit cannot silently close a dispute |
| P0 | Durable discovery inbox and triage | Previously collected research survives feed rotation; blocked sources and unresolved items remain visible; duplicate mirrors do not inflate corroboration |
| P1 | Compact search-first catalog | Search by product, driver, hash, CVE, mechanism, function and source; URL-shareable filters; accessible keyboard operation; explicit empty states |
| P1 | Consistent system dossiers | Every system exposes the same component/research outline and visible gaps, without inventing missing architecture |
| P1 | Source and version diffs | Show what changed and which claims need re-review, not just a new commit SHA or star count |
| P1 | Correction/update RSS and saved queries | Readers can subscribe to changes; bookmarks/watchlists work locally without accounts and can be exported |
| P2 | Version-scoped comparison views | Compare documented mechanisms/builds, displaying unknowns rather than ranking anti-cheat strength |
| P2 | Evidence-backed relationship explorer | Draw only documented edges, each opening its supporting source; retain a table alternative |
| P2 | Static full-text indexing | Introduce a build-generated index such as Pagefind when the catalog outgrows client-side card filtering; no search backend required |
| P2 | Reproducibility workspace | Record authorized lab configuration, tool versions, expected/observed behavior and bounded negative results, isolated from collection/deployment |

Avoid accounts, a discussion forum, a public arbitrary-URL crawler, exploit hosting and a graph-first homepage. They add operational burden without improving the evidence model.

## 5. Simplify the UI

Recommendation: **yes—keep the visual identity, make the application quieter and denser.** Dark graphite and a restrained accent can stay; the catalog should behave like a reference tool rather than a launch page.

- Four primary destinations: **Catalog, Systems, Research, Updates**. Place methodology, coverage, data exports and publishing under secondary navigation. Projects become a Research filter; editorial notes remain identifiable as notes.
- Make the landing view a search box, useful filters, a compact record table and recent substantive corrections. Remove the oversized hero, repeated project/note lists and vanity counters from the reading path.
- Default result columns: item, system/component, topic/type, evidence/claim state, applicable build and last review. Put star counts and repository trivia inside project details, not beside research-quality signals.
- A system dossier starts with a short scope statement and component inventory. Use predictable sections: Overview, Components, Mechanisms, Findings, Research and History. Preserve stable deep links and an accessible outline instead of loading every detail into a giant card.
- At the top of a claim or project, show what is asserted, which build it concerns, who reported it, whether it is disputed and what this catalog actually checked. Keep full caveats available next to the evidence, not hidden in a footer.
- Use readable body type and monospace only for identifiers/code. Support adequate contrast, keyboard focus, reduced motion and a light theme. On mobile, collapse filters and outlines; wide tables scroll within their own region.
- Do not replace sourced architecture with decorative arrows. A component map is useful only when its edges have evidence.

UI acceptance: a reader can find a named driver, see its scoped responsibilities, distinguish a reported weakness from a reproduced result, and open the original source without scanning multiple promotional sections. Test common phone, tablet and desktop widths, real filter interactions and downloads—not screenshots alone.

## 6. Delivery order (implemented)

1. **Evidence migration:** define the claim/source/build/correction contracts, migrate the existing 52 records and 9 notes, remove obsolete fields only after all callers/exports move, and seed the EAC dispute as the first contradiction case.
2. **Deep dossier pilot:** complete the EAC and Ironshield outline using inspected public evidence. Publish specific gaps and revision limits; do not equate a filled paragraph with completed research.
3. **Maintenance automation:** durable inbox, canonicalization, source-change detection, correction priority and GitHub-native reviewable updates. Retain the existing Pages deployment route.
4. **UI simplification:** compact catalog and four-destination navigation, uniform dossiers and visible evidence/claim states. Remove duplicated content after the new views work end to end.
5. **Coverage expansion:** repeat the pilot standard across the remaining systems. Use static search, comparisons and subscriptions without weakening the underlying evidence contract.

Each stage must ship complete behavior, migrated callers/exports, structural validation and browser smoke proof. Do not publish a placeholder "deep dossier" with guessed mechanisms.

## Publication and rights

Catalog publicly disclosed research, root causes and provenance. A purported leak can have a metadata record stating authenticity, public source and uncertainty; public availability does not authorize mirroring stolen source, proprietary dumps, credentials, personal data or undisclosed vulnerabilities. Do not turn a research reference into a live bypass service. Preserve vendor disclosure and remediation uncertainty. Choose explicit licenses for this project's own code and original content before claiming redistribution rights; third-party material retains its own terms.

`astro.config.mjs`:

```mjs
import { defineConfig } from "astro/config";

const site = process.env.SITE_URL?.trim();
const configuredBase = process.env.BASE_PATH?.trim() || "/";
if (site && (!/^https?:\/\//i.test(site) || !URL.canParse(site))) {
  throw new Error("SITE_URL must be an absolute http(s) URL");
}
if (!configuredBase.startsWith("/") || /[?#]/.test(configuredBase)) {
  throw new Error(
    "BASE_PATH must be a root-relative path, such as / or /repo/",
  );
}
const base = configuredBase.replace(/\/+$/, "") || "/";

export default defineConfig({
  ...(site ? { site } : {}),
  base,
  output: "static",
  trailingSlash: "never",
  vite: { server: { fs: { strict: true } } },
});

`scripts/digest.mjs`:

```mjs
import { readFile, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
const location = new URL("../src/data/discovery.json", import.meta.url);
const snapshot = JSON.parse(await readFile(location, "utf8"));
const generatedAt = new Date().toISOString();
const previous = snapshot.digest?.generatedAt;
const from = previous && +new Date(previous) <= +new Date(generatedAt) ? previous : new Date(Date.now() - 7 * 86_400_000).toISOString();
const within = (value) => value && +new Date(value) > +new Date(from) && +new Date(value) <= +new Date(generatedAt);
snapshot.digest = {
  generatedAt,
  from,
  to: generatedAt,
  addedIds: snapshot.items.filter((item) => within(item.firstSeen)).map((item) => item.id).sort(),
  changeIds: snapshot.changes.filter((change) => within(change.date)).map((change) => change.id).sort(),
  blockedSourceIds: snapshot.sources.filter((source) => source.state === "blocked").map((source) => source.id).sort(),
};
await writeFile(location, `${JSON.stringify(snapshot, null, 2)}\n`);
console.log(`Digest ${from} to ${generatedAt}: ${snapshot.digest.addedIds.length} discoveries, ${snapshot.digest.changeIds.length} changes, ${snapshot.digest.blockedSourceIds.length} blocked sources.`);

`scripts/discovery-helpers.mjs`:

```mjs
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import { XMLParser } from "fast-xml-parser";
import { parse } from "parse5";

export const hash = (value) => createHash("sha256").update(value).digest("hex").slice(0, 20);
const tracking = /^(utm_.+|fbclid|gclid|dclid|msclkid|mc_[ce]id|igshid|ref_src|spm)$/i;
export function canonicalUrl(value) {
  const parsed = new URL(value);
  if (parsed.protocol !== "https:") throw new Error(`Only HTTPS URLs are permitted: ${value}`);
  parsed.hash = "";
  parsed.hostname = parsed.hostname.toLowerCase();
  for (const key of [...parsed.searchParams.keys()]) if (tracking.test(key)) parsed.searchParams.delete(key);
  parsed.searchParams.sort();
  if (parsed.pathname !== "/") parsed.pathname = parsed.pathname.replace(/\/+$/, "");
  return parsed.href;
}
/** Exclude known profile/taxonomy URLs; an eligible URL is still only an unreviewed lead. */
export function isPublicationCandidate(value) {
  try {
    const url = new URL(value), path = url.pathname.replace(/\/+$/, "");
    if (url.protocol !== "https:") return false;
    if (/(?:^|\.)github\.com$/.test(url.hostname)) return path.split("/").filter(Boolean).length >= 2;
    if (/(?:^|\.)(?:x|twitter|vxtwitter|fxtwitter)\.com$/.test(url.hostname) || /^nitter\./.test(url.hostname)) return /\/status\/\d+(?:\/|$)/.test(path);
    if (/^\/(?:(?:blog|forum)\/)?(?:authors?|researchers?|profiles?|members?|users?|tags?|categor(?:y|ies)|about|contact)(?:\.(?:php|html?))?(?:\/|$)/i.test(path)) return false;
    return !/^\/(?:blog|archive|archives|posts|page)(?:\/(?:page\/)?\d+)?$/i.test(path);
  } catch { return false; }
}
export const identity = (url) => `item-${hash(canonicalUrl(url))}`;
export const short = (value, length = 280) => String(value ?? "").replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim().slice(0, length);
export function text(value) {
  if (value == null) return "";
  if (typeof value === "string" || typeof value === "number") return short(String(value).replace(/<[^>]*>/g, " "), 500);
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return text(value[0]);
  return text(value["#text"] ?? value.__cdata ?? value.content ?? "");
}
const parser = new XMLParser({ ignoreAttributes: false, attributeNamePrefix: "@_", textNodeName: "#text", cdataPropName: "__cdata", processEntities: true, removeNSPrefix: true, parseTagValue: false });
export function xml(body) { return parser.parse(body); }
export function feedItems(body, base) {
  const doc = xml(body);
  const entries = doc.rss?.channel?.item ?? doc.feed?.entry ?? doc.RDF?.item ?? [];
  if (!doc.rss && !doc.feed && !doc.RDF) throw new Error("Response is not RSS or Atom");
  return (Array.isArray(entries) ? entries : [entries]).map((entry) => {
    const links = Array.isArray(entry.link) ? entry.link : [entry.link];
    const link = links.find((candidate) => candidate?.["@_rel"] === "alternate") ?? links.find((candidate) => !candidate?.["@_rel"]);
    const guid = entry.guid?.["@_isPermaLink"] !== "false" && /^https:\/\//i.test(text(entry.guid)) ? text(entry.guid) : "";
    const url = (typeof link === "string" ? link : link?.["@_href"] || text(link)) || guid;
    const date = entry.pubDate ?? entry.published ?? entry.updated ?? entry.date;
    const parsedDate = date ? new Date(text(date)) : null;
    try {
      if (!url) return null;
      const resolved = canonicalUrl(new URL(url, base).href);
      return { url: resolved, title: text(entry.title), summary: short(text(entry.summary ?? entry.description ?? entry.encoded ?? entry.content), 350) || null, published: parsedDate && !Number.isNaN(+parsedDate) ? parsedDate.toISOString().slice(0, 10) : null };
    } catch { return null; }
  }).filter((item) => item?.title);
}
export function sitemapUrls(body, base) {
  const doc = xml(body);
  const root = doc.urlset?.url ?? doc.sitemapindex?.sitemap ?? [];
  if (!doc.urlset && !doc.sitemapindex) throw new Error("Response is not a sitemap");
  const values = Array.isArray(root) ? root : [root];
  return { index: Boolean(doc.sitemapindex), urls: values.map((item) => {
    try { const location = text(item.loc); return location ? { url: canonicalUrl(new URL(location, base).href), modified: text(item.lastmod) || null } : null; }
    catch { return null; }
  }).filter(Boolean) };
}
/** Approved dated article indexes only; never collect author profiles or follow article links. */
export function archiveItems(body, base) {
  const host = new URL(base).hostname;
  const items = new Map();
  const visit = (node, fn) => { fn(node); for (const child of node.childNodes ?? []) visit(child, fn); };
  const content = (node) => node.nodeName === "#text" ? node.value : ["script", "style"].includes(node.tagName) ? "" : (node.childNodes ?? []).map(content).join("");
  visit(parse(body), (node) => {
    if (node.tagName !== "article") return;
    let item = null, date = null;
    visit(node, (child) => {
      if (child.tagName === "time" && !date) date = child.attrs.find((attr) => attr.name === "datetime")?.value ?? null;
      if (child.tagName !== "a" || item) return;
      const href = child.attrs.find((attr) => attr.name === "href")?.value;
      if (!href) return;
      try {
        const url = canonicalUrl(new URL(href, base).href);
        const target = new URL(url), title = short(content(child), 160);
        if (target.hostname === host && /^\/(?:19|20)\d{2}\/\d{2}\/\d{2}\/[^/]+/.test(target.pathname) && title) item = { url, title, summary: null, published: null };
      } catch { /* Non-public or malformed locations are not discovery entries. */ }
    });
    if (item) {
      const published = date ? new Date(date) : null;
      item.published = published && !Number.isNaN(+published) ? published.toISOString().slice(0, 10) : null;
      items.set(item.url, item);
    }
  });
  return [...items.values()];
}
export function pageMetadata(body) {
  const scrub = (value) => short(value.replace(/<[^>]*>/g, " ").replace(/&(?:amp|nbsp|quot|#39|lt|gt);/g, " "), 220);
  const headings = [...body.matchAll(/<h[1-3]\b[^>]*>([\s\S]*?)<\/h[1-3]>/gi)].slice(0, 14).map((match) => scrub(match[1])).filter(Boolean);
  const title = scrub(body.match(/<title\b[^>]*>([\s\S]*?)<\/title>/i)?.[1] ?? "");
  const description = body.match(/<meta\b(?=[^>]*\bname=["']description["'])(?=[^>]*\bcontent=["']([^"']*)["'])[^>]*>/i)?.[1] ?? body.match(/<meta\b(?=[^>]*\bproperty=["']og:description["'])(?=[^>]*\bcontent=["']([^"']*)["'])[^>]*>/i)?.[1] ?? "";
  return [...new Set([title, scrub(description), ...headings].filter(Boolean))].slice(0, 16);
}
export function linesDiff(before, after) {
  const old = new Set(before);
  const next = new Set(after);
  return { added: after.filter((line) => !old.has(line)).slice(0, 16), removed: before.filter((line) => !next.has(line)).slice(0, 16) };
}
export function priorityFor(item, records) {
  const title = `${item.title} ${item.summary ?? ""}`.toLowerCase();
  if (/\b(corrections?|corrected|errata|retract(?:ed|ions?)?|disput(?:e|ed|es|ing)|incorrect|inaccurate)\b/.test(title)) return "correction";
  if (/\b(fix(?:ed|es)?|patch(?:ed|es)?|vulnerabilit(?:y|ies)|cve-\d{4}-\d+|advisor(?:y|ies))\b/.test(title)) return "fix";
  if (/\b(update|revision|release|changed|drift)\b/.test(title) && item.recordIds.length) return "drift";
  if (item.recordIds.length || item.claimIds.length || item.systemIds.length || /anti.?cheat|devirtualiz|kernel|driver|hypervisor|reverse.engineer|virtualiz|protect|obfuscat/i.test(title)) return "research";
  const productNames = records.filter((record) => record.kind === "product").map((record) => record.title.toLowerCase());
  if (productNames.some((name) => name.length > 5 && title.includes(name))) return "research";
  return "background";
}

`scripts/discovery.mjs`:

```mjs
import { readFile, readdir, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { archiveItems, canonicalUrl, feedItems, hash, identity, isPublicationCandidate, linesDiff, pageMetadata, priorityFor, short, sitemapUrls } from "./discovery-helpers.mjs";

const root = new URL("../src/data/", import.meta.url);
const file = (name) => new URL(name, root);
const load = async (name, fallback) => readFile(file(name), "utf8").then(JSON.parse).catch((error) => { if (error.code === "ENOENT") return fallback; throw error; });
const save = async (name, data) => writeFile(file(name), `${JSON.stringify(data, null, 2)}\n`);
const force = process.argv.includes("--force");
const backfill = process.argv.includes("--backfill");
if (process.argv.slice(2).some((flag) => !["--force", "--backfill"].includes(flag))) throw new Error("Supported options: --force, --backfill");
const now = new Date().toISOString();
const emptyDigest = { generatedAt: now, from: now, to: now, addedIds: [], changeIds: [], blockedSourceIds: [] };
const config = await load("discovery-sources.json", []);
if (!config.length) throw new Error("Discovery source registry must not be empty");
const initialStatus = (source) => ({ id: source.id, name: source.name, url: source.url, state: "pending", lastAttempt: null, lastSuccess: null, httpStatus: null, error: null, itemCount: 0, backfill: { state: "pending", inspectedFrom: null, inspectedThrough: null, detail: "No historical endpoint inspected; latest feed is not historical coverage." } });
const snapshot = await load("discovery.json", { schemaVersion: "2.0.0", syncedAt: now, sources: [], items: [], repos: [], changes: [], digest: emptyDigest });
const state = await load("discovery-state.json", { pages: {} });
state.publications ??= {};
/** Older snapshots recorded a never-attempted source as an error with an empty date; keep that meaning honest on load. */
for (const entry of snapshot.sources) {
  if (entry.lastAttempt === "") entry.lastAttempt = null;
  if (entry.lastAttempt === null && entry.httpStatus === null && entry.state === "error") { entry.state = "pending"; entry.error = null; }
}
const oldItems = new Map();
for (const item of snapshot.items) {
  if (!isPublicationCandidate(item.canonicalUrl) || (item.url !== item.canonicalUrl && !isPublicationCandidate(item.url))) continue;
  if (item.mirrors.length) item.mirrors = item.mirrors.filter(isPublicationCandidate);
  oldItems.set(item.canonicalUrl, item);
}
const sourceStatuses = new Map(snapshot.sources.map((entry) => [entry.id, entry]));
const repos = new Map(snapshot.repos.map((repo) => [repo.id, repo]));
const changes = new Map(snapshot.changes.map((change) => [change.id, change]));
const records = await Promise.all((await readdir(file("records"))).filter((name) => name.endsWith(".json")).map((name) => load(`records/${name}`, null)));
const knowledgeSources = await load("knowledge/sources.json", []);
const claims = await load("knowledge/claims.json", []);
const normalized = new Map();
function indexUrl(url, source) {
  if (!url) return;
  try { const key = canonicalUrl(url); if (!normalized.has(key)) normalized.set(key, []); normalized.get(key).push(source); }
  catch { /* Inaccessible/non-HTTPS citations cannot be polled. */ }
}
for (const source of knowledgeSources) { indexUrl(source.url, source); indexUrl(source.retrievalUrl, source); }
const refs = new Map();
for (const claim of claims) for (const citation of claim.citations ?? []) {
  const ids = [citation.sourceId];
  const source = knowledgeSources.find((entry) => entry.id === citation.sourceId);
  if (source) ids.push(source.originId);
  for (const id of ids) {
    if (!refs.has(id)) refs.set(id, { claimIds: new Set(), recordIds: new Set() });
    const ref = refs.get(id); ref.claimIds.add(claim.id);
    for (const recordId of claim.recordIds ?? []) ref.recordIds.add(recordId);
  }
}
function affected(url, sourceId, recordId = null) {
  const urls = normalized.get(canonicalUrl(url)) ?? [];
  const group = new Set([sourceId, ...urls.flatMap((source) => [source.id, source.originId])]);
  const recordIds = new Set(recordId ? [recordId] : []), claimIds = new Set();
  for (const id of group) { const ref = refs.get(id); if (!ref) continue; for (const entry of ref.claimIds) claimIds.add(entry); for (const entry of ref.recordIds) recordIds.add(entry); }
  for (const record of records) {
    if (!record?.repoUrl || canonicalUrl(record.repoUrl) !== canonicalUrl(url)) continue;
    recordIds.add(record.id);
    for (const claim of claims) if (claim.recordIds.includes(record.id)) claimIds.add(claim.id);
  }
  return { recordIds: [...recordIds].sort(), claimIds: [...claimIds].sort() };
}
function origin(url) {
  const sources = normalized.get(canonicalUrl(url)) ?? [];
  const source = sources.find((entry) => entry.transport !== "mirror") ?? sources[0] ?? null;
  if (source?.transport === "mirror") return knowledgeSources.find((entry) => entry.transport !== "mirror" && entry.originId === source.originId) ?? source;
  return source;
}
const productAliases = new Map([
  ["easy-anti-cheat", ["easy anti cheat", "easyanticheat", "eac"]],
  ["vanguard", ["riot vanguard", "vanguard"]],
  ["ea-javelin", ["ea javelin", "ea anticheat"]],
  ["anti-cheat-expert", ["tencent ace", "anti cheat expert"]],
  ["ricochet", ["ricochet anti cheat"]],
]);
function mentionedProducts(entry) {
  const haystack = ` ${`${entry.title} ${entry.summary ?? ""}`.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, " ")} `;
  return records.filter((record) => record?.kind === "product" && [
    ...(productAliases.get(record.id) ?? []),
    record.title.replace(/\([^)]*\)/g, "").trim().toLowerCase(),
    ...(record.aliases ?? []).map((alias) => alias.toLowerCase()),
  ].some((alias) => alias.length >= 3 && haystack.includes(` ${alias.replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, " ").trim()} `))).map((record) => record.id);
}
function registerItem(entry, source, refreshMetadata = true) {
  const observed = canonicalUrl(entry.url);
  const knownSource = origin(observed);
  const canonical = knownSource ? canonicalUrl(knownSource.url) : observed;
  if (!isPublicationCandidate(observed) || (canonical !== observed && !isPublicationCandidate(canonical))) return;
  const current = oldItems.get(canonical) ?? oldItems.get(observed);
  const refs = affected(canonical, knownSource?.id ?? source.id, source.kind === "github" ? source.id : null);
  const item = current ?? { id: identity(canonical), url: observed, canonicalUrl: canonical, title: entry.title, summary: entry.summary ?? null, sourceId: source.id, originId: knownSource?.originId ?? identity(canonical), systemIds: source.systemIds, topics: source.topics, published: entry.published ?? null, firstSeen: now, lastSeen: now, review: "unreviewed", priority: "background", recordIds: [], claimIds: [], mirrors: [] };
  item.lastSeen = now;
  if (refreshMetadata && observed === canonical) {
    const before = state.publications[canonical];
    const title = entry.title || item.title;
    const summary = short(entry.summary ?? item.summary, 350) || null;
    const after = [title, summary ?? ""].filter(Boolean);
    const next = hash(after.join("\n"));
    // A new fingerprint is a baseline, not proof that an upstream publication changed.
    if (before) addChange({ sourceId: knownSource?.id ?? source.id, kind: "content", before: before.hash, after: next, summary: "Publication metadata changed against its previously collected fingerprint; inspect linked claims before relying on their previous interpretation.", sourceUrl: canonical, diff: linesDiff(before.lines, after) });
    state.publications[canonical] = { hash: next, lines: after };
    item.title = title;
    item.summary = summary;
  }
  if (!item.published && entry.published) item.published = entry.published;
  const products = mentionedProducts(item);
  item.recordIds = [...new Set([...item.recordIds, ...refs.recordIds, ...products])].sort();
  item.claimIds = [...new Set([...item.claimIds, ...refs.claimIds])].sort();
  item.systemIds = [...new Set([...item.systemIds, ...source.systemIds, ...products])].sort();
  item.topics = [...new Set([...item.topics, ...source.topics])].sort();
  if (observed !== canonical) item.mirrors = [...new Set([...item.mirrors, observed])].sort();
  item.priority = priorityFor(item, records);
  oldItems.set(canonical, item);
  if (observed !== canonical) oldItems.delete(observed);
}
function addChange({ sourceId, date = now, kind, before, after, summary, sourceUrl, compareUrl, diff, recordId }) {
  if (before === after || (!diff.added.length && !diff.removed.length)) return;
  const id = `change-${hash(`${sourceId}|${kind}|${before}|${after}${kind === "availability" ? `|${date}` : ""}`)}`;
  if (changes.has(id)) return;
  const linked = affected(sourceUrl, sourceId, recordId);
  changes.set(id, { id, sourceId, date, kind, before, after, summary, ...linked, review: "pending", sourceUrl, ...(compareUrl ? { compareUrl } : {}), diff });
}
for (const source of config) {
  if (!source.id || !["rss", "github", "page"].includes(source.kind) || !source.originId || !Array.isArray(source.systemIds) || !Array.isArray(source.topics) || !Array.isArray(source.backfillEndpoints) || !source.scope || !(source.intervalHours > 0)) throw new Error(`Invalid registry source ${source.id}`);
  for (const value of [source.url, source.endpoint, ...source.backfillEndpoints]) canonicalUrl(value);
  if (!sourceStatuses.has(source.id)) sourceStatuses.set(source.id, initialStatus(source));
}
function refreshReviewedCommits() {
  for (const source of config.filter((candidate) => candidate.kind === "github")) {
    const repo = repos.get(source.id); if (!repo) continue;
    const record = records.find((entry) => entry?.repoUrl && canonicalUrl(entry.repoUrl) === canonicalUrl(source.url));
    repo.recordId = record?.id ?? null;
    repo.reviewedCommit = record?.reviewedCommit ?? null;
    repo.drift = Boolean(repo.reviewedCommit && repo.headSha && repo.reviewedCommit !== repo.headSha);
  }
}
// Only explicitly configured public HTTPS endpoints can be requested; sitemap descendants stay on the configured host.
function allowed(url, endpoint) {
  const parsed = new URL(canonicalUrl(url)), base = new URL(endpoint);
  if (parsed.hostname !== base.hostname || /^(localhost|.*\.local|127\.|10\.|192\.168\.|169\.254\.|172\.(1[6-9]|2\d|3[01])\.)/.test(parsed.hostname)) throw new Error(`Endpoint outside configured public host: ${url}`);
}
async function request(url, endpoint, accept = "text/plain", limit = 2_000_000, method = "GET") {
  allowed(url, endpoint);
  let target = url;
  for (let redirects = 0; redirects < 3; redirects++) {
    const response = await fetch(target, { method, redirect: "manual", signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15_000), headers: { "User-Agent": "anti-cheat-observatory/2.0 (metadata research discovery)", Accept: accept, ...(process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN && new URL(target).hostname === "api.github.com" ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN}` } : {}) } });
    if ([301, 302, 303, 307, 308].includes(response.status)) { target = new URL(response.headers.get("location"), target).href; allowed(target, endpoint); continue; }
    if (!response.ok) { const error = new Error(`HTTP ${response.status}`); error.httpStatus = response.status; throw error; }
    if (method === "HEAD") return { body: "", status: response.status, headers: response.headers };
    const reader = response.body?.getReader();
    if (!reader) throw new Error("Response has no body");
    const chunks = [];
    let count = 0;
    try {
      for (;;) {
        const { done, value } = await reader.read();
        if (done) break;
        count += value.length;
        if (count > limit) { await reader.cancel(); throw new Error("Response exceeds metadata size limit"); }
        chunks.push(value);
      }
    } finally { reader.releaseLock(); }
    const bytes = new Uint8Array(count);
    let offset = 0;
    for (const chunk of chunks) { bytes.set(chunk, offset); offset += chunk.length; }
    return { body: new TextDecoder().decode(bytes), status: response.status, headers: response.headers };
  }
  throw new Error("Too many redirects");
}
async function getJson(url, endpoint) { const response = await request(url, endpoint, "application/vnd.github+json"); return { value: JSON.parse(response.body), status: response.status }; }
const inspectedDate = (dates) => dates.map((date) => date?.slice(0, 10)).filter((date) => /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(date)).sort();
async function inspectBackfill(source, status) {
  if (!source.backfillEndpoints.length) { status.backfill = { state: "blocked", inspectedFrom: null, inspectedThrough: null, detail: "No approved historical endpoint; recent feed only, not a historical archive." }; return; }
  try {
    let count = 0, archiveCount = 0, complete = true;
    const dates = [];
    if (source.kind === "github") {
      const first = source.backfillEndpoints[0];
      for (let page = 1; page <= 3; page++) {
        const target = new URL(first); target.searchParams.set("per_page", "100"); target.searchParams.set("page", String(page));
        const { value } = await getJson(target.href, source.endpoint);
        if (!Array.isArray(value)) throw new Error("Expected GitHub commit history");
        for (const commit of value) {
          const date = commit.commit?.author?.date ?? null;
          dates.push(date);
          registerItem({ url: commit.html_url, title: short(commit.commit?.message?.split("\n")[0] ?? "Commit", 160), summary: null, published: date?.slice(0, 10) ?? null }, source);
          count++;
        }
        if (value.length < 100) break;
        if (page === 3) complete = false;
      }
    } else {
      const queue = source.backfillEndpoints.map((url) => ({ url, depth: 0 }));
      let inspected = 0;
      while (queue.length && inspected < 8 && count < 300) {
        const { url, depth } = queue.shift();
        const { body, headers } = await request(url, source.endpoint, "application/xml,text/xml,text/html"); inspected++;
        if (headers.get("content-type")?.toLowerCase().includes("text/html")) {
          const entries = archiveItems(body, source.url);
          if (!entries.length) throw new Error("Approved HTML index contained no dated article links");
          complete = false;
          for (const entry of entries) {
            allowed(entry.url, source.endpoint);
            registerItem(entry, source, false);
            dates.push(entry.published); count++; archiveCount++;
            if (count >= 300) break;
          }
          continue;
        }
        const sitemap = sitemapUrls(body, source.url);
        for (const entry of sitemap.urls) {
          allowed(entry.url, source.endpoint);
          if (sitemap.index) { if (depth < 1) queue.push({ url: entry.url, depth: depth + 1 }); else complete = false; }
          else if (new URL(entry.url).pathname !== "/" && isPublicationCandidate(entry.url)) {
            const path = new URL(entry.url).pathname.split("/").filter(Boolean).pop() ?? "";
            registerItem({ url: entry.url, title: short(decodeURIComponent(path).replace(/[-_]/g, " "), 160) || entry.url, summary: null, published: null }, source, false);
            count++;
            if (count >= 300) break;
          }
        }
      }
      if (queue.length || count >= 300) complete = false;
    }
    const range = inspectedDate(dates);
    status.backfill = { state: complete ? "complete" : "partial", inspectedFrom: range[0] ?? null, inspectedThrough: range.at(-1) ?? null, detail: source.kind === "github" ? `Inspected ${count} public commits, up to 3 pages; ${complete ? "API history ended" : "older history remains uninspected"}. Dates describe returned commits, not coverage of unpublished work.` : `Inspected ${count} URLs from approved indexes, including ${archiveCount} dated HTML article links; ${complete ? "declared sitemap exhausted" : "other archive pages or URLs remain uninspected"}. Dates, where present, are index-reported publication dates; sitemap lastmod is not publication evidence. Article bodies were not inspected.` };
  } catch (error) {
    status.backfill = { ...status.backfill, state: [401, 403, 429].includes(error.httpStatus) ? "blocked" : "partial", detail: `${status.backfill.detail} Historical inspection failed: ${short(error.message, 140)}` };
  }
}
async function poll(source) {
  if (source.kind === "rss") {
    const { body, status: code } = await request(source.endpoint, source.endpoint, "application/rss+xml,application/atom+xml,application/xml,text/xml", 8_000_000);
    const items = feedItems(body, source.url);
    if (!items.length) throw new Error("Feed returned no parseable entries");
    for (const item of items.slice(0, 100)) registerItem(item, source);
    return { status: code, count: items.length };
  }
  if (source.kind === "page") {
    const path = new URL(source.endpoint).pathname;
    const pdf = /\.pdf$/i.test(path);
    const json = /\.json$/i.test(path);
    const response = await request(source.endpoint, source.endpoint, pdf ? "application/pdf" : json ? "application/json" : "text/html", 1_000_000, pdf ? "HEAD" : "GET");
    const lines = pdf
      ? ["etag", "last-modified", "content-length"].map((key) => response.headers.get(key) ? `${key}: ${short(response.headers.get(key), 120)}` : "").filter(Boolean)
      : json
        ? (() => { const value = JSON.parse(response.body); return [short(value.cveMetadata?.cveId ?? value.title ?? "", 120), ...(value.containers?.cna?.descriptions ?? []).slice(0, 3).map((entry) => short(entry.value, 220))].filter(Boolean); })()
        : pageMetadata(response.body);
    if (!lines.length) throw new Error(pdf ? "Document provides no public version headers; binary not downloaded" : "No bounded text metadata could be inspected");
    const previous = state.pages[source.id];
    const next = hash([...lines].sort().join("\n"));
    if (previous && previous.hash !== next) addChange({ sourceId: source.id, kind: "content", before: previous.hash, after: next, summary: pdf ? "Document HTTP version headers changed; binary was not downloaded or examined." : "Publisher title, description or headings changed; inspect linked claims against the source.", sourceUrl: source.url, diff: linesDiff(previous.lines, lines) });
    state.pages[source.id] = { hash: next, lines };
    return { status: response.status, count: 0 };
  }
  const { value: repo, status: code } = await getJson(source.endpoint, source.endpoint);
  const { value: commit } = await getJson(`${source.endpoint}/commits/${encodeURIComponent(repo.default_branch ?? "HEAD")}`, source.endpoint);
  if (!commit.sha || !repo.html_url) throw new Error("Missing repository head metadata");
  const record = records.find((entry) => entry?.repoUrl && canonicalUrl(entry.repoUrl) === canonicalUrl(source.url));
  const previous = repos.get(source.id);
  const reviewedCommit = record?.reviewedCommit ?? null;
  const next = { id: source.id, name: source.name, url: source.url, recordId: record?.id ?? null, headSha: commit.sha, headDate: commit.commit?.author?.date ?? null, headMessage: short(commit.commit?.message?.split("\n")[0] ?? "", 220) || null, pushedAt: repo.pushed_at ?? null, stars: Number.isInteger(repo.stargazers_count) ? repo.stargazers_count : null, language: repo.language ?? null, license: repo.license?.spdx_id ?? null, description: short(repo.description, 300) || null, archived: Boolean(repo.archived), reviewedCommit, drift: Boolean(reviewedCommit && reviewedCommit !== commit.sha), stale: false };
  repos.set(source.id, next);
  if (previous?.headSha && previous.headSha !== next.headSha) {
    const compareUrl = `${source.url}/compare/${previous.headSha}...${next.headSha}`;
    let lines = { added: [`Head commit subject (not a patch): ${next.headMessage ?? next.headSha}`], removed: [`Previous commit subject (not a patch): ${previous.headMessage ?? previous.headSha}`] };
    try {
      const { value } = await getJson(`${source.endpoint}/compare/${previous.headSha}...${next.headSha}`, source.endpoint);
      const patches = (value.files ?? []).slice(0, 12).flatMap((entry) => (entry.patch ?? "").split("\n").filter((line) => /^[+-](?![+-])/.test(line)).slice(0, 6).map((line) => `${entry.filename}: ${short(line, 160)}`));
      if (patches.length) lines = { added: patches.filter((line) => /: \+/.test(line)).slice(0, 16), removed: patches.filter((line) => /: -/.test(line)).slice(0, 16) };
    } catch (error) { lines.added.push(`Compare unavailable: ${short(error.message, 90)}; inspect linked source`); }
    addChange({ sourceId: source.id, kind: "upstream", before: previous.headSha, after: next.headSha, summary: `Repository head changed from ${previous.headSha.slice(0, 12)} to ${next.headSha.slice(0, 12)}; unreviewed upstream change, not an updated reviewed commit.`, sourceUrl: source.url, compareUrl, diff: lines, recordId: record?.id });
  }
  let count = 0;
  for (const resource of ["releases?per_page=30", "issues?state=all&sort=updated&direction=desc&per_page=30"]) {
    const { value: entries } = await getJson(`${source.endpoint}/${resource}`, source.endpoint);
    if (!Array.isArray(entries)) throw new Error(`Expected a public repository ${resource.split("?")[0]} list`);
    for (const entry of entries.slice(0, 30)) {
      if (!entry.html_url || entry.draft || entry.pull_request) continue;
      const release = resource.startsWith("releases");
      const title = release ? `Release: ${entry.name || entry.tag_name}` : `Public issue: ${entry.title}`;
      if (!release && !entry.title) continue;
      registerItem({ url: entry.html_url, title: short(title, 160), summary: short(entry.body, 350) || null, published: (entry.published_at ?? entry.created_at)?.slice(0, 10) ?? null }, source);
      count++;
    }
  }
  return { status: code, count };
}
for (const source of config) {
  const status = sourceStatuses.get(source.id);
  const due = force || !status.lastAttempt || !Number.isFinite(+new Date(status.lastAttempt)) || Date.now() - +new Date(status.lastAttempt) >= source.intervalHours * 3_600_000;
  const previousState = status.state;
  const previouslyAttempted = Boolean(status.lastAttempt);
  if (due) {
    try {
      const result = await poll(source);
      Object.assign(status, { name: source.name, url: source.url, state: "ok", httpStatus: result.status, lastAttempt: now, lastSuccess: now, error: null, itemCount: result.count });
    } catch (error) {
      const code = error.httpStatus ?? null;
      Object.assign(status, { name: source.name, url: source.url, state: [401, 403, 429].includes(code) ? "blocked" : "error", httpStatus: code, lastAttempt: now, error: short(error.message, 200) });
      if (repos.has(source.id)) repos.set(source.id, { ...repos.get(source.id), stale: true });
      console.warn(`${source.id}: ${status.state} (${status.error}); retaining earlier discoveries`);
    }
    if (previouslyAttempted && previousState !== status.state) {
      addChange({ sourceId: source.id, kind: "availability", before: previousState, after: status.state, summary: `Source access changed from ${previousState} to ${status.state}; previously retained material remains subject to re-review.`, sourceUrl: source.url, diff: { added: [status.state === "ok" ? `Reachable as of ${now}` : `${status.state}: ${status.error}`], removed: [previousState] } });
    }
  }
  if (backfill) await inspectBackfill(source, status);
}
refreshReviewedCommits();
snapshot.syncedAt = now;
snapshot.sources = [...sourceStatuses.values()];
snapshot.items = [...new Set(oldItems.values())].sort((a, b) => (b.published ?? b.firstSeen).localeCompare(a.published ?? a.firstSeen) || a.id.localeCompare(b.id));
const retainedIds = new Set(snapshot.items.map((item) => item.id));
snapshot.digest.addedIds = snapshot.digest.addedIds.filter((id) => retainedIds.has(id));
snapshot.repos = [...repos.values()];
snapshot.changes = [...changes.values()].sort((a, b) => b.date.localeCompare(a.date) || a.id.localeCompare(b.id));
await save("discovery-state.json", state);
await save("discovery.json", snapshot);
console.log(`Discovery: ${snapshot.items.length} retained items, ${snapshot.changes.length} changes, ${snapshot.sources.filter((entry) => entry.state !== "ok").length} unavailable sources.`);
