`scripts/import-proposal.mjs`:

```mjs
import { readFile, writeFile, mkdir, open, rename, rm } from "node:fs/promises";
import path from "node:path";
import { pathToFileURL } from "node:url";
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { projectRoot, readJson, readKnowledge, arrayCollections, directoryCollections } from "./knowledge-io.mjs";
import { validateDataset, validateProposal } from "./knowledge-validation.mjs";
import { mergeProposal } from "../src/lib/proposal.ts";

const readExisting = (filename) => readFile(filename, "utf8").catch((error) => { if (error.code === "ENOENT") return null; throw error; });

/** Merge a fully checked proposal without publishing partially validated entities. */
export async function importProposal(proposal, { root = projectRoot, replace = false, dryRun = false } = {}) {
  const lockPath = path.join(root, ".aco-import.lock");
  let lock;
  try { lock = await open(lockPath, "wx"); }
  catch (error) { if (error.code === "EEXIST") throw new Error("Another import holds .aco-import.lock. Do not remove it while an import is running."); throw error; }
  const staged = [];
  const committed = [];
  try {
    const existing = await readKnowledge(root);
    const errors = [...validateDataset(existing), ...validateProposal(proposal, existing, replace)];
    if (errors.length) throw new Error(`Proposal rejected before writing:\n${errors.join("\n")}`);
    const merged = mergeProposal(proposal, existing);
    const mergedErrors = validateDataset(merged);
    if (mergedErrors.length) throw new Error(`Merged catalog rejected:\n${mergedErrors.join("\n")}`);
    const writes = [];
    for (const collection of arrayCollections) if (proposal[collection]?.length) {
      writes.push({ filename: path.join(root, "src/data/knowledge", `${collection}.json`), body: JSON.stringify(merged[collection], null, 2) + "\n" });
    }
    for (const [collection, directory] of Object.entries(directoryCollections)) for (const entity of proposal[collection] ?? []) {
      writes.push({ filename: path.join(root, directory, `${entity.id}.json`), body: JSON.stringify(entity, null, 2) + "\n" });
    }
    const result = { dryRun, changedFiles: writes.map((entry) => path.relative(root, entry.filename).replaceAll("\\", "/")), counts: Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(proposal).filter(([key, value]) => key !== "schemaVersion" && Array.isArray(value)).map(([key, value]) => [key, value.length])) };
    if (dryRun) return result;
    const suffix = `.aco-${randomUUID()}.tmp`;
    for (const entry of writes) {
      await mkdir(path.dirname(entry.filename), { recursive: true });
      const original = await readExisting(entry.filename);
      const temporary = entry.filename + suffix;
      await writeFile(temporary, entry.body, { flag: "wx" });
      staged.push({ ...entry, temporary, original });
    }
    if (JSON.stringify(await readKnowledge(root)) !== JSON.stringify(existing)) throw new Error("Catalog changed during preparation; import stopped before replacement.");
    for (const entry of staged) { await rename(entry.temporary, entry.filename); committed.push(entry); }
    return result;
  } catch (error) {
    const recoveryErrors = [];
    for (const entry of committed.reverse()) {
      try {
        if (await readExisting(entry.filename) !== entry.body) throw new Error("File changed outside this import; not overwritten during recovery");
        if (entry.original === null) await rm(entry.filename);
        else await writeFile(entry.filename, entry.original);
      } catch (recoveryError) { recoveryErrors.push(`${entry.filename}: ${recoveryError.message}`); }
    }
    if (recoveryErrors.length) throw new Error(`${error.message}\nRecovery needs inspection:\n${recoveryErrors.join("\n")}`);
    throw error;
  } finally {
    await Promise.all(staged.map((entry) => rm(entry.temporary, { force: true })));
    await lock.close();
    await rm(lockPath);
  }
}

if (process.argv[1] && pathToFileURL(path.resolve(process.argv[1])).href === import.meta.url) {
  try {
    const args = process.argv.slice(2);
    if (args.some((arg) => arg.startsWith("--") && !["--replace", "--dry-run"].includes(arg))) throw new Error("Unknown option. Usage: npm run import -- proposal.json [--replace] [--dry-run]");
    const files = args.filter((arg) => !arg.startsWith("--"));
    if (files.length !== 1) throw new Error("Usage: npm run import -- proposal.json [--replace] [--dry-run]");
    const result = await importProposal(await readJson(path.resolve(files[0])), { replace: args.includes("--replace"), dryRun: args.includes("--dry-run") });
    console.log(JSON.stringify(result, null, 2));
    console.log(result.dryRun ? "Dry run passed; no catalog files changed." : "Proposal imported. Inspect the changes, build, exercise the affected pages, then commit to publish.");
  } catch (error) { console.error(error.message); process.exitCode = 1; }
}
```

`scripts/knowledge-io.mjs`:

```mjs
import { readFile, readdir } from "node:fs/promises";
import path from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

export const projectRoot = fileURLToPath(new URL("../", import.meta.url));
export const arrayCollections = ["sources", "claims", "builds", "mechanisms", "relationships", "corrections", "dossiers"];
export const directoryCollections = { records: "src/data/records", posts: "src/data/posts", validations: "src/data/knowledge/validations" };
export async function readJson(filename) {
  return JSON.parse(await readFile(filename, "utf8"));
}
export async function readKnowledge(root = projectRoot) {
  const data = { schemaVersion: "2.0.0" };
  for (const collection of arrayCollections) {
    data[collection] = await readJson(path.join(root, "src/data/knowledge", `${collection}.json`));
    if (!Array.isArray(data[collection])) throw new Error(`${collection}.json must contain an array`);
  }
  for (const [collection, directory] of Object.entries(directoryCollections)) {
    data[collection] = [];
    for (const filename of (await readdir(path.join(root, directory))).filter((name) => name.endsWith(".json")).sort()) {
      const entity = await readJson(path.join(root, directory, filename));
      if (path.basename(filename, ".json") !== entity.id) throw new Error(`${directory}/${filename}: filename must equal the entity ID`);
      data[collection].push(entity);
    }
  }
  return data;
}
```

`scripts/knowledge-validation.mjs`:

```mjs
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import Ajv from "ajv";
import addFormats from "ajv-formats";
import { knowledgeErrors, proposalErrors } from "../src/lib/proposal.ts";

export const schema = JSON.parse(await readFile(new URL("../src/data/knowledge.schema.json", import.meta.url), "utf8"));
const ajv = new Ajv({ allErrors: true });
addFormats(ajv);
const checkDataset = ajv.compile(schema);
const checkProposal = ajv.compile({ ...schema, $id: `${schema.$id}:proposal`, required: ["schemaVersion"] });
const shapeErrors = (check) => (check.errors ?? []).map((error) => `${error.instancePath || "/"}: ${error.message}${error.params?.additionalProperty ? ` (${error.params.additionalProperty})` : ""}`);
export function validateDataset(data) {
  return checkDataset(data) ? knowledgeErrors(data) : shapeErrors(checkDataset);
}
export function validateProposal(proposal, existing, replace = false) {
  if (!checkProposal(proposal)) return shapeErrors(checkProposal);
  if (!Object.entries(proposal).some(([key, value]) => key !== "schemaVersion" && Array.isArray(value) && value.length)) return ["Proposal must contain at least one entity"];
  return proposalErrors(proposal, existing, replace);
}

const absoluteHttps = (value) => { try { return new URL(value).protocol === "https:"; } catch { return false; } };
const timestamp = (value) => typeof value === "string" && !Number.isNaN(Date.parse(value));
/** Discovery remains unreviewed metadata; it may reference evidence, never alter it. */
export function validateDiscovery(snapshot, data, config) {
  const errors = [];
  if (!snapshot || snapshot.schemaVersion !== "2.0.0" || !timestamp(snapshot.syncedAt)) return ["Discovery snapshot requires schemaVersion 2.0.0 and a sync timestamp"];
  for (const key of ["sources", "items", "repos", "changes"]) if (!Array.isArray(snapshot[key])) errors.push(`discovery.${key} must be an array`);
  if (!Array.isArray(config) || !config.length) errors.push("Discovery registry must contain approved sources");
  if (errors.length) return errors;
  const systemIds = new Set(data.records.filter((record) => record.kind === "product").map((record) => record.id));
  const recordIds = new Set(data.records.map((record) => record.id));
  const claimIds = new Set(data.claims.map((claim) => claim.id));
  const configIds = new Set();
  for (const entry of config) {
    if (!entry || typeof entry.id !== "string" || configIds.has(entry.id)) { errors.push("Discovery registry has a missing/duplicate source ID"); continue; }
    configIds.add(entry.id);
    if (!["rss", "github", "page"].includes(entry.kind) || !absoluteHttps(entry.url) || !absoluteHttps(entry.endpoint)) errors.push(`${entry.id}: discovery needs approved HTTPS URLs and a valid acquisition method`);
    if (!Number.isFinite(entry.intervalHours) || entry.intervalHours <= 0) errors.push(`${entry.id}: invalid polling interval`);
    if (!Array.isArray(entry.backfillEndpoints) || entry.backfillEndpoints.some((url) => !absoluteHttps(url))) errors.push(`${entry.id}: invalid backfill endpoint`);
    if (!Array.isArray(entry.systemIds) || entry.systemIds.some((id) => !systemIds.has(id))) errors.push(`${entry.id}: unknown scoped system`);
    if (!entry.scope || !entry.originId) errors.push(`${entry.id}: source scope and origin are required`);
  }
  const statusIds = new Set();
  for (const status of snapshot.sources) {
    if (statusIds.has(status.id)) errors.push(`discovery: duplicate source ${status.id}`);
    statusIds.add(status.id);
    if (!configIds.has(status.id)) errors.push(`${status.id}: snapshot source is absent from the registry`);
    if (!["ok", "blocked", "error", "pending"].includes(status.state) || !absoluteHttps(status.url) || (status.lastAttempt !== null && !timestamp(status.lastAttempt)) || (status.lastSuccess !== null && !timestamp(status.lastSuccess))) errors.push(`${status.id}: invalid retrieval status`);
    if (status.state === "pending" && (status.lastAttempt !== null || status.httpStatus !== null)) errors.push(`${status.id}: a never-attempted source cannot report an attempt or HTTP status`);
    if (status.state === "ok" && status.lastSuccess === null) errors.push(`${status.id}: a reachable source must record its last successful retrieval`);
    if (!status.backfill || !["pending", "partial", "complete", "blocked"].includes(status.backfill.state) || typeof status.backfill.detail !== "string") errors.push(`${status.id}: backfill must record its inspected scope`);
  }
  const itemIds = new Set(); const canonicalUrls = new Set();
  const references = (entity) => {
    if (!Array.isArray(entity.recordIds) || entity.recordIds.some((id) => !recordIds.has(id))) errors.push(`${entity.id}: unknown discovery record`);
    if (!Array.isArray(entity.claimIds) || entity.claimIds.some((id) => !claimIds.has(id))) errors.push(`${entity.id}: unknown affected claim`);
  };
  for (const item of snapshot.items) {
    if (itemIds.has(item.id) || canonicalUrls.has(item.canonicalUrl)) errors.push(`${item.id}: duplicate discovery identity or canonical URL`);
    itemIds.add(item.id); canonicalUrls.add(item.canonicalUrl);
    if (!absoluteHttps(item.url) || !absoluteHttps(item.canonicalUrl) || !statusIds.has(item.sourceId) || !item.originId || !timestamp(item.firstSeen) || !timestamp(item.lastSeen)) errors.push(`${item.id}: invalid persistent discovery identity`);
    if (!["unreviewed", "linked", "dismissed"].includes(item.review) || !["correction", "fix", "drift", "research", "background"].includes(item.priority)) errors.push(`${item.id}: invalid review/priority state`);
    if (!Array.isArray(item.systemIds) || item.systemIds.some((id) => !systemIds.has(id))) errors.push(`${item.id}: unknown discovery system`);
    if (!Array.isArray(item.mirrors) || item.mirrors.some((url) => !absoluteHttps(url))) errors.push(`${item.id}: invalid mirror URL`);
    references(item);
  }
  const changeIds = new Set();
  for (const change of snapshot.changes) {
    if (changeIds.has(change.id)) errors.push(`${change.id}: duplicate source change`);
    changeIds.add(change.id);
    if (!statusIds.has(change.sourceId) || !["content", "upstream", "availability"].includes(change.kind) || !["pending", "reviewed"].includes(change.review) || !timestamp(change.date) || !absoluteHttps(change.sourceUrl)) errors.push(`${change.id}: invalid source change`);
    if (typeof change.before !== "string" || typeof change.after !== "string" || !change.diff || !Array.isArray(change.diff.added) || !Array.isArray(change.diff.removed)) errors.push(`${change.id}: substantive before/after evidence is required`);
    references(change);
  }
  const repoIds = new Set();
  for (const repo of snapshot.repos) {
    if (repoIds.has(repo.id)) errors.push(`${repo.id}: duplicate tracked repository`);
    repoIds.add(repo.id);
    if (repo.recordId && !recordIds.has(repo.recordId)) errors.push(`${repo.id}: repository points at an unknown record`);
    if (!absoluteHttps(repo.url) || (repo.headSha !== null && !/^[a-f0-9]{40}$/.test(repo.headSha)) || typeof repo.stale !== "boolean") errors.push(`${repo.id}: invalid repository metadata`);
  }
  const digest = snapshot.digest;
  if (!digest || !timestamp(digest.generatedAt) || !timestamp(digest.from) || !timestamp(digest.to)) errors.push("Discovery digest requires its real date range");
  else {
    if (!Array.isArray(digest.addedIds) || digest.addedIds.some((id) => !itemIds.has(id))) errors.push("Digest refers to unknown discoveries");
    if (!Array.isArray(digest.changeIds) || digest.changeIds.some((id) => !changeIds.has(id))) errors.push("Digest refers to unknown source changes");
    if (!Array.isArray(digest.blockedSourceIds) || digest.blockedSourceIds.some((id) => !statusIds.has(id))) errors.push("Digest refers to unknown blocked sources");
  }
  return errors;
}
```

`scripts/validate.mjs`:

```mjs
import path from "node:path";
import { projectRoot, readJson, readKnowledge } from "./knowledge-io.mjs";
import { validateDataset, validateDiscovery } from "./knowledge-validation.mjs";

try {
  const data = await readKnowledge();
  const errors = validateDataset(data);
  if (!errors.length) {
    const discovery = await readJson(path.join(projectRoot, "src/data/discovery.json"));
    const registry = await readJson(path.join(projectRoot, "src/data/discovery-sources.json"));
    errors.push(...validateDiscovery(discovery, data, registry));
    const outlets = await readJson(path.join(projectRoot, "src/data/research-sources.json"));
    if (!Array.isArray(outlets) || !outlets.length || new Set(outlets.map((outlet) => outlet.id)).size !== outlets.length) errors.push("Research publication directory must contain unique entries");
    else for (const outlet of outlets) {
      if (!URL.canParse(outlet.url) || new URL(outlet.url).protocol !== "https:" || !["Independent research", "Community forum", "Vendor documentation", "Academic"].includes(outlet.type) || !["Public", "Partially accessible"].includes(outlet.access) || !outlet.limitation) errors.push(`${outlet.id}: invalid publication-directory metadata`);
    }
  }
  if (errors.length) { console.error(errors.join("\n")); process.exitCode = 1; }
  else {
    const counts = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(data).filter(([key, value]) => key !== "schemaVersion" && Array.isArray(value)).map(([key, value]) => [key, value.length]));
    console.log(`Validated normalized knowledge 2.0.0: ${JSON.stringify(counts)}`);
    console.log("Evidence origins, scopes, references, disputes, execution contracts and discovery integrity passed. Structural validation does not establish binary semantics.");
  }
} catch (error) {
  console.error(`Validation failed: ${error.message}`);
  process.exitCode = 1;
}
```

```astro
import type { CatalogRecord } from "../lib/knowledge-types";
import { trackedRepos } from "../lib/discovery";

interface Props {
  record: CatalogRecord;
}
const { record } = Astro.props;
const repo = trackedRepos.find((entry) => entry.recordId === record.id);
const shortSha = (sha: string) => sha.slice(0, 12);
const reviewedCommit = record.reviewedCommit;
const rows = [
  { label: "Language", value: repo?.language ?? record.repoLanguage },
  { label: "License", value: repo?.license && repo.license !== "NOASSERTION" ? repo.license : record.repoLicense },
  { label: "Stars at last snapshot", value: repo?.stars != null ? String(repo.stars) : null },
  { label: "Reviewed commit", value: reviewedCommit ? shortSha(reviewedCommit) : null },
  { label: "Upstream head", value: repo?.headSha ? shortSha(repo.headSha) : null },
  { label: "Last upstream push", value: repo?.pushedAt ? repo.pushedAt.slice(0, 10) : null },
];
---

<section class="panel repo-panel" aria-labelledby="repo-title">
  <h2 id="repo-title">Upstream repository</h2>
  {record.repoUrl && <p><a href={record.repoUrl} target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">{record.repoUrl}</a></p>}
  <dl class="repo-facts">
    {rows.filter((row) => row.value != null).map((row) => (
      <div><dt>{row.label}</dt><dd class="mono">{row.value}</dd></div>
    ))}
  </dl>
  {repo?.drift && repo.headSha && reviewedCommit && (
    <p class="repo-alert"><strong>Upstream moved since the reviewed commit.</strong> The tracked head <code>{shortSha(repo.headSha)}</code> differs from <code>{shortSha(reviewedCommit)}</code>. Findings are scoped to the reviewed revision until rechecked.</p>
  )}
  {repo?.stale && <p class="muted">Snapshot stale: the last fetch did not refresh upstream metadata.</p>}
  {repo?.headMessage && <p class="muted">Latest upstream commit: {repo.headMessage}{repo.headDate ? ` (${repo.headDate.slice(0, 10)})` : ""}</p>}
  <p class="muted">Repository counts and activity are secondary context, not evidence that the research claims have been independently reproduced.</p>
</section>

<style>
  .repo-panel { min-width: 0; }
  .repo-panel h2 { margin: 0 0 .7rem; }
  .repo-panel p { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
  .repo-facts { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit,minmax(10rem,1fr)); gap: .7rem 1.2rem; margin: 1rem 0; }
  .repo-facts div { min-width: 0; }
  .repo-facts dt { color: var(--muted, #9aa9af); font-size: .85rem; }
  .repo-facts dd { margin: .2rem 0; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
  .repo-alert { border-left: 3px solid #d7a65a; padding-left: .8rem; }
</style>
```

```ts
import { recordKinds, type CatalogRecord, type RecordKind } from "./knowledge-types";

export { recordKinds } from "./knowledge-types";
const modules = import.meta.glob<{ default: CatalogRecord }>("../data/records/*.json", { eager: true });
export const records: CatalogRecord[] = Object.values(modules)
  .map((module) => module.default)
  .sort((a, b) => recordKinds.indexOf(a.kind) - recordKinds.indexOf(b.kind) || a.title.localeCompare(b.title));
const recordIndex = new Map(records.map((record) => [record.id, record]));
export const kindLabels: Record<RecordKind, string> = {
  product: "Systems", component: "Components", technique: "Techniques", finding: "Findings", project: "Projects",
};
export const kindNames: Record<RecordKind, string> = {
  product: "System dossier", component: "Component", technique: "Technique", finding: "Finding", project: "Research project",
};
export const countKind = (kind: RecordKind) => records.filter((record) => record.kind === kind).length;
export const recordById = (id: string) => recordIndex.get(id);
export const recordsByIds = (ids: string[]) => ids.flatMap((id) => recordIndex.has(id) ? [recordIndex.get(id)!] : []);
export const products = () => records.filter((record) => record.kind === "product");
/** Editorial browsing links are not evidence of implementation or architectural edges. */
export function relatedTo(id: string, kind: RecordKind): CatalogRecord[] {
  const origin = recordIndex.get(id);
  return records.filter((record) => record.kind === kind && (record.relatedIds.includes(id) || origin?.relatedIds.includes(record.id)));
}
export const componentsForProduct = (id: string) => relatedTo(id, "component");
export const projectsForProduct = (id: string) => relatedTo(id, "project");
export function recordsForProduct(id: string): CatalogRecord[] {
  const origin = recordIndex.get(id);
  return records.filter((record) => record.id !== id && record.kind !== "product" && (origin?.relatedIds.includes(record.id) || record.relatedIds.includes(id)));
}
export const sectionId = (title: string, index: number) => `section-${index}-${title.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, "-").replace(/^-|-$/g, "")}`;
export const dataset = () => ({ schemaVersion: "2.0.0", name: "Anti-Cheat Observatory", description: "Version-scoped research records. Evidence and claim states are separate from independent reproduction.", records });
export const csv = () => {
  const fields = ["id", "kind", "title", "vendor", "historical", "updated", "platforms", "layers", "filenames", "cves", "buildIds", "mechanismIds", "sourceIds", "repoUrl", "reviewedCommit", "summary"] as const;
  const cell = (value: unknown) => `"${String(value ?? "").replaceAll('"', '""')}"`;
  return [fields.map(cell).join(","), ...records.map((record) => fields.map((field) => cell(Array.isArray(record[field]) ? (record[field] as string[]).join(" | ") : record[field])).join(","))].join("\r\n");
};
```

```ts
export const claimsForPost = (id: string) => claims.filter((claim) => claim.postIds.includes(id));
```

`src/lib/paths.ts`:

```ts
const base = `/${import.meta.env.BASE_URL.replace(/^\/+|\/+$/g, "")}`.replace(
  /^\/$/,
  "",
);

/** Prefix an internal root-relative URL with the configured Astro base path. */
export function withBase(path: string): string {
  if (
    path.startsWith("#") ||
    path.startsWith("?") ||
    /^(?:[a-z][a-z\d+.-]*:|\/\/)/i.test(path)
  )
    return path;
  if (!path.startsWith("/"))
    throw new TypeError("withBase expects a root-relative path");
  if (!base) return path;
  return `${base}${path}`;
}

const configuredRepository = import.meta.env.PUBLIC_REPOSITORY;
const validRepository = /^[a-z\d](?:[a-z\d-]{0,37}[a-z\d])?\/[a-z\d_.-]+$/i;
export const repositoryUrl: string | undefined =
  configuredRepository &&
  validRepository.test(configuredRepository) &&
  ![".", ".."].includes(configuredRepository.split("/")[1])
    ? `https://github.com/${configuredRepository}`
    : undefined;
export const repositoryBranch: string =
  import.meta.env.PUBLIC_REPOSITORY_BRANCH || "main";

/** Return a real repository edit URL, or nothing when this build has no repository. */
export function editUrl(file: string): string | undefined {
  if (!repositoryUrl) return undefined;
  const segments = file.split("/");
  if (
    !segments.length ||
    segments.some((segment) => !segment || segment === "." || segment === "..")
  )
    return undefined;
  return `${repositoryUrl}/edit/${encodeURIComponent(repositoryBranch)}/${segments.map(encodeURIComponent).join("/")}`;
}
```

`src/lib/proposal.ts`:

```ts
import type { KnowledgeDataset, KnowledgeProposal, Claim, ValidationRecord } from "./knowledge-types.ts";

const collections = ["records", "posts", "sources", "claims", "builds", "mechanisms", "validations", "relationships", "corrections"] as const;
const aspectIds = ["deployment", "components", "interfaces", "mechanisms", "protection", "findings", "research", "history"];
const worksheetIds = ["trigger", "context", "inputs", "outputs", "conditions", "protected-object", "primitives", "dependencies", "validation", "counterexamples"];
const https = (value: string) => { try { return new URL(value).protocol === "https:"; } catch { return false; } };

/** Semantic validation after JSON Schema shape validation. Shared by browser proposals and CLI imports. */
export function knowledgeErrors(data: KnowledgeDataset): string[] {
  const errors: string[] = [];
  const allIds = new Set<string>();
  for (const key of collections) {
    for (const entity of data[key]) {
      if (allIds.has(entity.id)) errors.push(`${key}: duplicate global ID ${entity.id}`);
      allIds.add(entity.id);
    }
  }
  const records = new Map(data.records.map((entity) => [entity.id, entity]));
  const posts = new Map(data.posts.map((entity) => [entity.id, entity]));
  const sources = new Map(data.sources.map((entity) => [entity.id, entity]));
  const claims = new Map(data.claims.map((entity) => [entity.id, entity]));
  const builds = new Map(data.builds.map((entity) => [entity.id, entity]));
  const mechanisms = new Map(data.mechanisms.map((entity) => [entity.id, entity]));
  const validations = new Map(data.validations.map((entity) => [entity.id, entity]));
  const systems = new Set(data.records.filter((record) => record.kind === "product").map((record) => record.id));
  const refs = (owner: string, ids: string[], index: { has(id: string): boolean }, label: string) => {
    for (const id of ids) if (!index.has(id)) errors.push(`${owner}: unknown ${label} ${id}`);
  };
  const observed = (validation: ValidationRecord | undefined, activity: string, claim?: Claim) => Boolean(validation && validation.authority === "observed" && validation.performedBy === "observatory" && validation.authorized && validation.activity === activity && validation.executedAt && (!claim || validation.claimIds.includes(claim.id)));
  for (const source of data.sources) {
    if (!https(source.url) || (source.retrievalUrl && !https(source.retrievalUrl))) errors.push(`${source.id}: source URLs must be absolute HTTPS`);
    if (source.revision.kind === "git" && !/^[a-f0-9]{40}$/.test(source.revision.value ?? "")) errors.push(`${source.id}: git revision must be a full commit SHA`);
    if (source.revision.kind === "unversioned" && source.revision.value !== null) errors.push(`${source.id}: unversioned sources cannot claim an immutable revision`);
    if (source.transport === "mirror" && (!source.originId || source.originId === source.id)) errors.push(`${source.id}: a mirror must identify its original evidence origin`);
    if (/^https:\/\/(?:www\.)?(?:x\.com|twitter\.com)\//i.test(source.url) && !/^https:\/\/(?:www\.)?(?:x\.com|twitter\.com)\/[^/]+\/status\/\d+/i.test(source.url)) errors.push(`${source.id}: researcher profiles are not evidence citations`);
  }
  for (const record of data.records) {
    refs(record.id, record.relatedIds, records, "record");
    refs(record.id, record.sourceIds, sources, "source");
    refs(record.id, record.buildIds, builds, "build");
    refs(record.id, record.mechanismIds, mechanisms, "mechanism");
    if (record.relatedIds.includes(record.id)) errors.push(`${record.id}: a record cannot relate to itself`);
    if (record.kind === "project" && !record.repoUrl) errors.push(`${record.id}: project repository URL is required`);
    if (record.kind !== "project" && (record.repoUrl || record.reviewedCommit || record.repoLicense || record.repoLanguage)) errors.push(`${record.id}: repository fields belong to projects`);
    if (record.historical && record.kind !== "finding") errors.push(`${record.id}: historical flag is reserved for findings`);
    for (const section of record.sections) {
      refs(record.id, section.claimIds, claims, "claim");
      for (const id of section.claimIds) if (claims.has(id) && !claims.get(id)!.recordIds.includes(record.id)) errors.push(`${record.id}: section claim ${id} must identify its record`);
    }
  }
  for (const post of data.posts) {
    refs(post.id, post.productIds, systems, "system"); refs(post.id, post.relatedIds, records, "record"); refs(post.id, post.sourceIds, sources, "source");
    if (post.updated < post.published) errors.push(`${post.id}: update date precedes publication`);
    for (const section of post.sections) {
      refs(post.id, section.claimIds, claims, "claim");
      for (const id of section.claimIds) if (claims.has(id) && !claims.get(id)!.postIds.includes(post.id)) errors.push(`${post.id}: section claim ${id} must identify its post`);
    }
  }
  for (const claim of data.claims) {
    refs(claim.id, claim.recordIds, records, "record"); refs(claim.id, claim.postIds, posts, "post"); refs(claim.id, claim.systemIds, systems, "system"); refs(claim.id, claim.buildIds, builds, "build"); refs(claim.id, claim.mechanismIds, mechanisms, "mechanism"); refs(claim.id, claim.validationIds, validations, "validation"); refs(claim.id, claim.contradicts, claims, "contradictory claim"); refs(claim.id, claim.supersedes, claims, "superseded claim");
    if (!claim.recordIds.length && !claim.postIds.length) errors.push(`${claim.id}: claim must be linked to a record or note`);
    if ([...claim.contradicts, ...claim.supersedes].includes(claim.id)) errors.push(`${claim.id}: self-contradiction/supersession is not allowed`);
    const supportingOrigins = new Set<string>();
    let accessible = false;
    for (const citation of claim.citations) {
      const source = sources.get(citation.sourceId);
      if (!source) { errors.push(`${claim.id}: unknown citation source ${citation.sourceId}`); continue; }
      if (citation.locator.url && !https(citation.locator.url)) errors.push(`${claim.id}: citation locator must use HTTPS`);
      if (citation.locator.kind === "function" && !citation.locator.addressSpace) errors.push(`${claim.id}: function locator needs an address space`);
      if (citation.relation === "supports") supportingOrigins.add(source.originId);
      if (source.access === "available") accessible = true;
    }
    if (["observation", "inference"].includes(claim.kind) && !claim.citations.some((citation) => citation.relation !== "context")) errors.push(`${claim.id}: factual claim needs attributed supporting or contradicting evidence`);
    if (claim.state === "corroborated" && supportingOrigins.size < 2) errors.push(`${claim.id}: corroboration needs at least two independent origins, not mirrors`);
    if (claim.state === "disputed" && !claim.contradicts.length && !claim.citations.some((citation) => citation.relation === "contradicts") && !data.claims.some((other) => other.contradicts.includes(claim.id))) errors.push(`${claim.id}: disputed claim needs an explicit challenge`);
    if (claim.state === "refuted" && !claim.citations.some((citation) => citation.relation === "contradicts") && !data.claims.some((other) => other.contradicts.includes(claim.id) && other.review !== "collected" && !["refuted", "superseded"].includes(other.state) && other.citations.some((citation) => citation.relation === "supports"))) errors.push(`${claim.id}: refutation needs attributed counterevidence, not merely a new state label`);
    if (claim.state === "superseded" && !data.claims.some((other) => other.supersedes.includes(claim.id))) errors.push(`${claim.id}: superseded claim needs a replacement claim`);
    if (claim.review === "source-inspected" && claim.kind === "observation" && !accessible) errors.push(`${claim.id}: inaccessible original text cannot be source-inspected evidence`);
    if (["artifact-inspected", "behavior-reproduced"].includes(claim.review)) {
      const matching = claim.validationIds.map((id) => validations.get(id)).filter((value): value is ValidationRecord => Boolean(value));
      if (!matching.some((validation) => observed(validation, claim.review, claim) && (
        claim.review !== "behavior-reproduced" || (
          validation.status === "pass" &&
          validation.buildId !== null &&
          claim.buildIds.includes(validation.buildId) &&
          (builds.get(validation.buildId)?.hashes.length ?? 0) > 0
        )
      ))) errors.push(`${claim.id}: ${claim.review} requires one matching authorized execution record and a hashed sample in the claim scope`);
    }
  }
  for (const build of data.builds) {
    refs(build.id, build.recordIds, records, "record"); refs(build.id, build.systemIds, systems, "system"); refs(build.id, build.sourceIds, sources, "source");
    for (const hash of build.hashes) {
      if (hash.origin === "source-reported" && (!hash.sourceId || !sources.has(hash.sourceId))) errors.push(`${build.id}: source-reported hash requires an identifiable source`);
      if (hash.origin === "project-computed") {
        const validation = validations.get(hash.validationId ?? "");
        if (!observed(validation, "artifact-inspected") || validation?.status !== "pass" || validation?.buildId !== build.id) errors.push(`${build.id}: a computed hash requires a matching observed artifact-validation record`);
      }
    }
  }
  for (const mechanism of data.mechanisms) {
    refs(mechanism.id, mechanism.systemIds, systems, "system"); refs(mechanism.id, mechanism.recordIds, records, "record"); refs(mechanism.id, mechanism.buildIds, builds, "build"); refs(mechanism.id, mechanism.claimIds, claims, "claim");
    if (new Set(mechanism.worksheet.map((row) => row.topic)).size !== worksheetIds.length || worksheetIds.some((topic) => !mechanism.worksheet.some((row) => row.topic === topic))) errors.push(`${mechanism.id}: all technical worksheet topics are required exactly once`);
    for (const row of mechanism.worksheet) {
      refs(mechanism.id, row.claimIds, claims, "worksheet claim");
      if (!row.claimIds.length && !row.unknown?.trim()) errors.push(`${mechanism.id}: ${row.topic} must have evidence or an explicit unknown`);
      if (row.claimIds.some((id) => !mechanism.claimIds.includes(id))) errors.push(`${mechanism.id}: worksheet evidence must belong to the mechanism's claims`);
    }
  }
  for (const validation of data.validations) {
    refs(validation.id, validation.claimIds, claims, "claim"); refs(validation.id, validation.sourceIds, sources, "source");
    if (validation.buildId && !builds.has(validation.buildId)) errors.push(`${validation.id}: unknown validation build ${validation.buildId}`);
    if (validation.authority === "observed") {
      if (!validation.authorized || validation.performedBy !== "observatory" || !validation.executedAt || validation.status === "reported") errors.push(`${validation.id}: observed work requires authorization, Observatory performer, execution date and observed result`);
      if (validation.activity === "behavior-reproduced" && (!validation.buildId || !(builds.get(validation.buildId)?.hashes.length))) errors.push(`${validation.id}: observed execution needs a hashed sample`);
    } else if (validation.status === "pass") errors.push(`${validation.id}: an external author's passing tests must be labeled reported, not our observed pass`);
    if (validation.executedAt && validation.executedAt.slice(0, 10) > validation.reviewedAt) errors.push(`${validation.id}: review cannot predate execution`);
  }
  for (const relationship of data.relationships) {
    refs(relationship.id, [relationship.fromId, relationship.toId], allIds, "relationship endpoint"); refs(relationship.id, relationship.claimIds, claims, "evidence claim");
    if (relationship.fromId === relationship.toId) errors.push(`${relationship.id}: self-edge is not a documented relationship`);
    if (!relationship.claimIds.some((id) => { const claim = claims.get(id); return claim && ["observation", "inference"].includes(claim.kind) && claim.citations.length > 0; })) errors.push(`${relationship.id}: graph edges need factual evidence, not browsing links`);
  }
  for (const correction of data.corrections) {
    refs(correction.id, correction.recordIds, records, "record"); refs(correction.id, correction.claimIds, claims, "claim"); refs(correction.id, correction.sourceIds, sources, "source");
    for (const id of correction.resolutionEvidenceIds) if (!claims.has(id) && !validations.has(id)) errors.push(`${correction.id}: resolution evidence must identify a claim or validation record`);
    if (correction.kind === "dispute" && correction.status === "resolved" && !correction.resolutionEvidenceIds.length) errors.push(`${correction.id}: a dispute cannot be resolved merely by an upstream commit`);
  }
  const dossierSystems = new Set<string>();
  for (const dossier of data.dossiers) {
    if (!systems.has(dossier.systemId)) errors.push(`${dossier.systemId}: unknown dossier system`);
    if (dossierSystems.has(dossier.systemId)) errors.push(`${dossier.systemId}: duplicate dossier`);
    dossierSystems.add(dossier.systemId);
    if (new Set(dossier.aspects.map((aspect) => aspect.id)).size !== aspectIds.length || aspectIds.some((id) => !dossier.aspects.some((aspect) => aspect.id === id))) errors.push(`${dossier.systemId}: all eight dossier aspects are required exactly once`);
    for (const aspect of dossier.aspects) {
      refs(dossier.systemId, aspect.claimIds, claims, "aspect claim");
      if (aspect.status === "documented" && !aspect.claimIds.length) errors.push(`${dossier.systemId}: documented ${aspect.id} needs evidence`);
      if (aspect.status !== "documented" && !aspect.questions.length) errors.push(`${dossier.systemId}: incomplete ${aspect.id} needs specific open questions`);
    }
  }
  for (const id of systems) if (!dossierSystems.has(id)) errors.push(`${id}: missing uniform system dossier`);
  return errors;
}

export function mergeProposal(proposal: KnowledgeProposal, existing: KnowledgeDataset): KnowledgeDataset {
  const merged = { ...existing };
  for (const key of collections) {
    const additions = proposal[key] ?? [];
    const replacements = new Map(additions.map((entry) => [entry.id, entry]));
    // All collections share identity but retain their concrete type at the dataset boundary.
    (merged as unknown as Record<string, unknown>)[key] = [...existing[key].filter((entry) => !replacements.has(entry.id)), ...additions];
  }
  const dossiers = new Map((proposal.dossiers ?? []).map((entry) => [entry.systemId, entry]));
  merged.dossiers = [...existing.dossiers.filter((entry) => !dossiers.has(entry.systemId)), ...(proposal.dossiers ?? [])];
  return merged;
}

export function proposalErrors(proposal: KnowledgeProposal, existing: KnowledgeDataset, replace = false): string[] {
  const errors: string[] = [];
  for (const key of collections) {
    const existingIds = new Set(existing[key].map((entry) => entry.id));
    const proposedIds = new Set<string>();
    for (const entity of proposal[key] ?? []) {
      if (proposedIds.has(entity.id)) errors.push(`${key}: duplicate proposed ID ${entity.id}`);
      proposedIds.add(entity.id);
      if (!replace && existingIds.has(entity.id)) errors.push(`${key}: ID ${entity.id} already exists; use an explicit replacement`);
    }
  }
  const dossierIds = new Set<string>();
  for (const dossier of proposal.dossiers ?? []) {
    if (dossierIds.has(dossier.systemId)) errors.push(`dossiers: duplicate proposed system ${dossier.systemId}`);
    dossierIds.add(dossier.systemId);
    if (!replace && existing.dossiers.some((entry) => entry.systemId === dossier.systemId)) errors.push(`dossiers: ${dossier.systemId} already exists; use an explicit replacement`);
  }
  return [...errors, ...knowledgeErrors(mergeProposal(proposal, existing))];
}
```

```ts
const modules = import.meta.glob<{ default: ResearchPost }>("../data/posts/*.json", { eager: true });

export const postsForRecord = (id: string) => posts.filter((post) => post.productIds.includes(id) || post.relatedIds.includes(id));
```

`src/lib/rss.ts`:

```ts
import { withBase } from "./paths";

export interface FeedEntry {
  title: string;
  path: string;
  date: string;
  summary: string;
  category: string;
}

const escape = (value: string) =>
  value.replaceAll("&", "&amp;").replaceAll("<", "&lt;").replaceAll(">", "&gt;").replaceAll('"', "&quot;");

/** Configure SITE_URL for absolute subscription links on the published static site. */
export function feedXml(
  origin: string | undefined,
  meta: { title: string; description: string; path: string },
  entries: FeedEntry[],
): string {
  const self = origin ? new URL(withBase(meta.path), origin).href : undefined;
  const items = entries
    .filter((entry) => !Number.isNaN(Date.parse(entry.date)))
    .map((entry) => {
      const link = origin ? new URL(withBase(entry.path), origin).href : withBase(entry.path);
      return [
        "    <item>",
        `      <title>${escape(entry.title)}</title>`,
        `      <link>${escape(link)}</link>`,
        `      <guid isPermaLink="false">${escape(`${entry.path}@${entry.date}`)}</guid>`,
        `      <category>${escape(entry.category)}</category>`,
        `      <pubDate>${new Date(entry.date).toUTCString()}</pubDate>`,
        `      <description>${escape(entry.summary)}</description>`,
        "    </item>",
      ].join("\n");
    })
    .join("\n");
  return [
    '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>',
    '<rss version="2.0" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom">',
    "  <channel>",
    `    <title>${escape(meta.title)}</title>`,
    `    <description>${escape(meta.description)}</description>`,
    `    <link>${escape(origin ? new URL(withBase("/"), origin).href : withBase("/"))}</link>`,
    self ? `    <atom:link href="${escape(self)}" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml" />` : "",
    items,
    "  </channel>",
    "</rss>",
    "",
  ]
    .filter((line) => line !== "")
    .join("\n");
}
```

```astro
    <header class="page-header editorial-header">
      <p class="eyebrow">About this reference</p>
      <h1>Anti-Cheat Observatory</h1>
      <p>A selected, public-source reference to anti-cheat systems, components and security research. Its job is to make the evidence and its limits easier to inspect—not to rank products or certify defenses. Historical findings are not advertised as working bypasses.</p>
    </header>

    <div class="editorial-body">
      <section id="scope">
        <h2>Purpose and scope</h2>
        <p>The <a href={withBase("/")}>catalog</a> connects system dossiers, technical claims, research notes and source records. The <a href={withBase("/reference")}>APIs &amp; binaries reference</a> groups documented and undocumented interfaces, research binaries and drivers by their catalog tags. Inclusion describes cited research or relevant interfaces, not ownership by an anti-cheat vendor, use in a particular deployment or effectiveness against a product.</p>
        <p>This is a curated selection, not an exhaustive system inventory or live status monitor. A missing item means the reference has not established it; it does not prove the capability or behavior is absent.</p>
      </section>

      <section id="evidence">
        <h2>Evidence standard</h2>
        <p>Substantive claims should identify a source and precise passage, the observation or inference it supports, applicable build or environment where known, and the limits of that support. The <a href={withBase("/methodology")}>methodology</a> distinguishes provenance, review activity and claim state; contextual citations do not independently corroborate a statement.</p>
        <p>Reading a source establishes what that source reports. It is not inspection of an identified binary, independent runtime reproduction or confirmation of current deployment. Source-reported versions and hashes are not project-computed measurements. Contradictions and unknowns remain visible rather than being resolved by assumption.</p>
      </section>

      <section id="research">
        <h2>Research versus discovery</h2>
        <p>Reviewed research records summarize accessible evidence with attribution, scope and explicit limitations. Discovery entries collect leads from public feeds, repository activity or indexes for possible later review. An item appearing in the <a href={withBase("/updates")}>updates</a> stream does not mean its underlying article, code or artifact has been inspected, nor does a metadata change establish that a product changed. Review and publication are separate steps.</p>
      </section>

      <section id="history">
        <h2>Historical and build limits</h2>
        <p>Reports about a particular version, build or historical incident stay bounded to that context. Product families and deployed configurations change; a past vulnerability does not establish current exposure, and a past observation is not evidence of an active bypass. Unspecified versions stay unspecified. Compare the cited source, its review date and the claim's applicability before drawing conclusions about a different environment.</p>
      </section>

      <section id="corrections">
        <h2>Corrections and contributions</h2>
        <p>If a citation, scope or interpretation is wrong, identify the affected record and claim, the exact source passage or counterevidence, and the version or environment to which the correction applies. The <a href={withBase("/publishing")}>publishing workspace</a> prepares an attributed proposal for local import; it does not submit or publish directly. Corrections should preserve the trace of earlier claims and their disputes rather than silently rewriting history.</p>
        {repositoryUrl && <p>To propose a change, <a href={`${repositoryUrl}/issues`} rel="noopener noreferrer">open a repository issue</a> or <a href={`${repositoryUrl}/pulls`} rel="noopener noreferrer">submit a pull request</a>. Do not include private telemetry, personal information, proprietary binaries or exploit payloads. For an undisclosed vulnerability, use the affected vendor's security reporting process first.</p>}
      </section>

      <section id="publishing">

        <p>The site is statically built with Astro for hosting on GitHub Pages; browsing it does not require an account or backend. Catalog edits are made in the repository, reviewed through its Git-backed workflow and published when the Pages workflow builds and deploys the default branch. The <a href={withBase("/updates")}>updates page</a> separates newly discovered source metadata from reviewed editorial material; publication is not a guarantee that third-party links remain accessible or that a claim still applies to current builds.</p>

      </section>
    </div>
  </div>
```

```astro
          <ol class="source-list">
            {sources.map((source) => (
              <li id={`source-${source.id}`}>
                <a href={withBase(`/sources/${source.id}`)}>{source.title}</a>
                <span class="muted"> · {source.author && `${source.author} / `}{source.publisher}{source.published && ` · Published ${source.published}`} · Accessed {source.accessed} · {source.provenance} · {source.access} · {source.revision.kind === "unversioned" ? "unversioned" : `${source.revision.kind}: ${source.revision.value}`}</span>
                <a href={source.url} target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" aria-label={`Read original: ${source.title}`}> ↗ Original</a>
              </li>
            ))}
          </ol>
        </section>
        <div class="panel">
          <p>Corrections should preserve attribution and historical scope.</p>
          {edit
            ? <a href={edit} target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Edit this note on GitHub ↗</a>
            : <a href={withBase("/publishing")}>Open the publishing workspace</a>}
        </div>
      </article>
      <aside class="note-aside">
        <nav class="panel" aria-label="Contents of this note">
          <h2>In this note</h2>
          <ul>
            <li><a href="#sources">Sources & provenance</a></li>
            {post.sections.map((section, index) => <li><a href={`#${sectionId(section.title, index)}`}>{section.title}</a></li>)}
          </ul>
        </nav>
        {related.length > 0 && <div class="panel">
          <h2>Related records</h2>
          <ul>{related.map((record) => <li><span class="muted">{kindNames[record.kind]} · </span><a href={withBase(`/records/${record.id}`)}>{record.title}</a></li>)}</ul>
        </div>}
        <div class="panel"><h2>Topics</h2><p>{post.tags.join(" · ")}</p></div>
        <a href={withBase("/methodology#limits")}>How we evaluate sources</a>
      </aside>
    </div>
    {otherPosts.length > 0 && <section class="related-notes">
      <h2>Further reading</h2>
      <div class="grid">{otherPosts.map((entry) => <PostCard post={entry} />)}</div>
      <p><a href={withBase("/blog")}>All research notes →</a></p>
    </section>}
  </div>
</Layout>
```

```astro
---
import Layout from "../layouts/Layout.astro";
import { products } from "../lib/catalog";
import { dossierForSystem } from "../lib/knowledge";
import { dossierAspects } from "../lib/knowledge-types";
import { withBase } from "../lib/paths";

const labels: Record<(typeof dossierAspects)[number], string> = {
  deployment: "Deployment",
  components: "Components",
  interfaces: "Interfaces",
  mechanisms: "Mechanisms",
  protection: "Protection",
  findings: "Findings",
  research: "Research",
  history: "History",
};
const systems = products().map((record) => ({ record, dossier: dossierForSystem(record.id) }));
const count = (status: "documented" | "partial" | "unknown") =>
  systems.reduce(
    (total, { dossier }) => total + (dossier?.aspects.filter((aspect) => aspect.status === status).length ?? 0),
    0,
  );
const unmapped = systems.reduce(
  (total, { dossier }) => total + dossierAspects.length - (dossier?.aspects.length ?? 0),
  0,
);
---

<Layout title="Coverage map" active="systems" description="Eight-aspect research dossier coverage for each cataloged system, including explicit unknown and unassessed gaps.">
  <div class="page-container coverage-page" data-pagefind-body>
    <header class="page-header">
      <p class="muted">Research coverage / not a product rating</p>
      <h1>Coverage &amp; open questions</h1>
      <p>Each cell reports the editorial state of one aspect of a system dossier. A gap means the available catalog has not established an answer; it never establishes the absence of a feature, flaw, or defense.</p>
    </header>

    <section class="panel" aria-label="Coverage totals">
      <div class="coverage-summary">
        <span><strong>{systems.length}</strong> systems</span>
        <span><strong>{count("documented")}</strong> documented aspects</span>
        <span><strong>{count("partial")}</strong> partial aspects</span>
        <span><strong>{count("unknown")}</strong> unknown aspects</span>
        {unmapped > 0 && <span><strong>{unmapped}</strong> unassessed aspects</span>}
      </div>
    </section>

    <section aria-labelledby="dossier-map">
      <h2 id="dossier-map">Eight-aspect dossier map</h2>
      <p class="muted">Open a system to read its underlying claims, citations, limitations and unresolved questions. Counts in documented and partial cells are linked claim counts, not evidence-quality scores.</p>
      <div class="table-wrap" role="region" tabindex="0" aria-label="Scrollable system coverage table">
        <table class="data-table">
          <caption class="sr-only">Editorial dossier status for eight aspects of each system; statuses do not measure security or effectiveness.</caption>
          <thead><tr><th scope="col">System</th>{dossierAspects.map((aspect) => <th scope="col">{labels[aspect]}</th>)}</tr></thead>
          <tbody>
            {systems.map(({ record, dossier }) => (
              <tr>
                <th scope="row"><a href={withBase(`/records/${record.id}`)}>{record.title}</a><small class="muted">{record.vendor}</small></th>
                {dossierAspects.map((id) => {

                  return <td>
                    {aspect ? <a href={withBase(`/records/${record.id}#${id}`)} aria-label={`${record.title}: ${labels[id]} ${aspect.status}, ${aspect.claimIds.length} linked claims`}>
                      <span class={`badge coverage-${aspect.status}`}>{aspect.status}</span>
                      {aspect.claimIds.length > 0 && <small class="muted">{aspect.claimIds.length} {aspect.claimIds.length === 1 ? "claim" : "claims"}</small>}
                    </a> : <span class="badge coverage-unassessed">unassessed</span>}
                  </td>;
                })}
              </tr>
            ))}
          </tbody>
        </table>
      </div>
    </section>

    <section class="panel coverage-guide" aria-labelledby="reading-map">
      <h2 id="reading-map">How to read the map</h2>
      <dl class="guide-grid">
        <div><dt>Documented</dt><dd>A dossier aspect has cited claims. This does not certify completeness, current deployment, or independent reproduction.</dd></div>
        <div><dt>Partial</dt><dd>Some claims are attached, but the dossier still identifies material open questions.</dd></div>
        <div><dt>Unknown</dt><dd>The dossier records insufficient support for an answer. Unknown is not a negative finding.</dd></div>
        <div><dt>Unassessed</dt><dd>No aspect entry exists in the catalog for this system. This is an editorial gap, not a product observation.</dd></div>
      </dl>
      <p class="muted">Aspect statuses summarize coverage only. A source's origin, review activity and the state of each individual claim remain separate. Cross-system counts are not rankings.</p>
      <a class="button" href={withBase("/methodology#evidence")}>Read the evidence methodology</a>
    </section>
  </div>
</Layout>
```

`src/pages/digest.xml.ts`:

```ts
import type { APIRoute } from "astro";
import { discovery, discoveryItems, discoveryChanges, discoverySources } from "../lib/discovery";
import { feedXml, type FeedEntry } from "../lib/rss";

/** The scheduled weekly digest: what discovery added, what changed, and what stayed blocked. */
export const GET: APIRoute = ({ site }) => {
  const digest = discovery.digest;
  const itemById = new Map(discoveryItems.map((item) => [item.id, item]));
  const changeById = new Map(discoveryChanges.map((change) => [change.id, change]));
  const sourceById = new Map(discoverySources.map((source) => [source.id, source]));
  const blocked = digest.blockedSourceIds.map((id) => sourceById.get(id)?.name ?? id);
  const entries: FeedEntry[] = [
    {
      title: `Weekly digest ${digest.from.slice(0, 10)} → ${digest.to.slice(0, 10)}`,
      path: "/updates#digest",
      date: digest.generatedAt,
      summary: `${digest.addedIds.length} newly discovered item(s), ${digest.changeIds.length} source change(s), ${digest.blockedSourceIds.length} blocked source(s)${blocked.length ? `: ${blocked.join(", ")}` : ""}. Discovery metadata is never promoted to a reviewed claim automatically.`,
      category: "digest",
    },
    ...digest.addedIds.flatMap((id) => {
      const item = itemById.get(id);
      return item ? [{
        title: `Discovered: ${item.title}`,
        path: `/feed#item-${item.id}`,
        date: item.firstSeen,
        summary: `${item.summary ?? "No summary available."} Priority: ${item.priority}. Review state: ${item.review}. Source: ${sourceById.get(item.sourceId)?.name ?? item.sourceId}.`,
        category: `discovery (${item.priority})`,
      }] : [];
    }),
    ...digest.changeIds.flatMap((id) => {
      const change = changeById.get(id);
      return change ? [{
        title: `Changed: ${sourceById.get(change.sourceId)?.name ?? change.sourceId}`,
        path: `/updates#change-${change.id}`,
        date: change.date,
        summary: `${change.summary} Review: ${change.review}.`,
        category: "source change",
      }] : [];
    }),
  ].sort((a, b) => b.date.localeCompare(a.date));
  return new Response(
    feedXml(site?.origin, {
      title: "Anti-Cheat Observatory — weekly digest",
      description: "Weekly discovery digest. Items are unreviewed metadata until a claim is revised with cited evidence.",
      path: "/digest.xml",
    }, entries),
    { headers: { "Content-Type": "application/rss+xml; charset=utf-8" } },
  );
};

```

```astro
import Layout from "../layouts/Layout.astro";
import { discovery, discoveryItems, discoverySources } from "../lib/discovery";
import { withBase } from "../lib/paths";

const sources = new Map(discoverySources.map((source) => [source.id, source]));
const sourceOptions = [...discoverySources].sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name));
const topics = [...new Set(discoveryItems.flatMap((item) => item.topics))].sort();
const systems = [...new Set(discoveryItems.flatMap((item) => item.systemIds))].sort();
const items = [...discoveryItems].sort((a, b) =>
  (b.published ?? b.firstSeen).localeCompare(a.published ?? a.firstSeen) || a.title.localeCompare(b.title),
);
const safeExternal = (value: string) => {
  try {
    const url = new URL(value);
    return url.protocol === "https:" || url.protocol === "http:" ? url.href : null;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
};
const dateLabel = (value: string | null) => {
  if (!value || Number.isNaN(Date.parse(value))) return "Not recorded";
  const date = new Date(value);
  return /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(value)
    ? date.toISOString().slice(0, 10)
    : `${date.toISOString().slice(0, 16).replace("T", " ")} UTC`;
};
const sourceState = { ok: "Reachable", blocked: "Blocked", error: "Fetch failed", pending: "Not yet collected" } as const;
const backfillState = { pending: "Pending", partial: "Partial", complete: "Complete", blocked: "Blocked" } as const;

<script>
  const form = document.querySelector<HTMLFormElement>("#feed-filters");
  if (form) {
    const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
    const fields = ["source", "priority", "review", "topic", "system"] as const;
    for (const key of fields) {
      const select = form.elements.namedItem(key);
      if (select instanceof HTMLSelectElement) {
        const value = params.get(key);
        if (value && [...select.options].some((option) => option.value === value)) select.value = value;
      }
    }
    const matches = (row: HTMLTableRowElement) => fields.every((key) => {
      const value = params.get(key);
      if (!value) return true;
      if (key === "topic" || key === "system") {
        const list = JSON.parse(row.dataset[key === "topic" ? "topics" : "systems"] ?? "[]") as string[];
        return list.includes(value);
      }
      return row.dataset[key] === value;
    });
    const rows = document.querySelectorAll<HTMLTableRowElement>("[data-feed-item]");
    let count = 0;
    for (const row of rows) {
      row.hidden = !matches(row);
      if (!row.hidden) count++;
    }
    const result = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#feed-result-count");
    if (result) result.textContent = `${count} of ${rows.length} items shown from the committed snapshot.`;
    const noResults = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#feed-no-results");
    if (noResults) noResults.hidden = count !== 0 || rows.length === 0;
  }
</script>
```

```astro
import Layout from "../layouts/Layout.astro";
import { records } from "../lib/catalog";
import { claimsForRecord } from "../lib/knowledge";
import { withBase } from "../lib/paths";

const techniques = records.filter((record) => record.kind === "technique");
const preferred = ["User mode", "Kernel", "Hardware", "Firmware", "Hypervisor", "Server", "Research"];
const tagged = new Set(techniques.flatMap((record) => record.layers));
const layers = [...preferred.filter((layer) => tagged.has(layer)), ...[...tagged].filter((layer) => !preferred.includes(layer)).sort()];
const layerNotes: Record<string, string> = {
  "User mode": "Applications, game processes and user-space client code.",
  Kernel: "Operating-system privileges, drivers and kernel interfaces.",
  Hardware: "Device and hardware interaction; not automatically a firmware claim.",
  Firmware: "Device or platform firmware and its execution context.",
  Hypervisor: "Virtual machine monitors and guest/host boundaries; distinct from code virtualization.",
  Server: "Game or service backend authority over client-provided actions.",
  Research: "Cross-cutting analysis tag, not an execution privilege level.",
};

        <table class="data-table trust-table">
          <caption class="sr-only">Technique records by editorial layer tags, with listed sources and linked claims. Marks do not establish product capabilities or bypasses.</caption>
          <thead><tr><th scope="col">Technique</th>{layers.map((layer) => <th scope="col">{layer}</th>)}<th scope="col">Claims</th><th scope="col">Sources</th></tr></thead>
          <tbody>
            {techniques.map((record) => <tr>
              <th scope="row"><a href={withBase(`/records/${record.id}`)}>{record.title}</a></th>
              {layers.map((layer) => <td class="matrix-cell">{record.layers.includes(layer)
                ? <span aria-label={`${layer} in study scope`} class="tagged">●</span>
                : <span aria-label={`${layer} not tagged`} class="muted">—</span>}</td>)}
              <td>{claimsForRecord(record.id).length}</td><td>{record.sourceIds.length}</td>
            </tr>)}
          </tbody>
        </table>
      </div>
    </section>

    <section class="panel" aria-labelledby="boundaries">
      <h2 id="boundaries">What the columns mean</h2>
      <dl class="layer-guide">
        {layers.map((layer) => <div><dt>{layer}</dt><dd>{layerNotes[layer] ?? "Layer label as used by the catalog record; read the record for its specific scope."}</dd></div>)}
      </dl>
      <p><strong>Trust boundaries are not capability scores.</strong> Layer tags do not say a product monitors that layer, a technique defeats a protection, or a project reproduced the behavior. No mark can be inferred from a repository's stars, commits or activity. Absence of a mark is not evidence that the layer is absent from an implementation.</p>
      <a class="button" href={withBase("/methodology#evidence")}>How claims are evaluated</a>
    </section>
  </div>
</Layout>
```

```astro
---
import Layout from "../layouts/Layout.astro";
import { withBase } from "../lib/paths";
---

<Layout title="Research methodology" active="research" description="Definitions of source provenance, review activity, claim state, applicability, discovery and rights for the anti-cheat research reference.">
  <div class="page-container method-page" data-pagefind-body>
    <header class="page-header">
      <p class="muted">Reading the evidence</p>
      <h1>Methodology &amp; limits</h1>
      <p>This is a selected, version-scoped research reference, not a bypass service, security certification or complete inventory of deployed products. Claims remain attached to specific citations and their limits.</p>
    </header>

    <nav class="panel method-nav" aria-label="On this page">
      <a href="#evidence">Evidence dimensions</a><a href="#provenance">Provenance</a><a href="#review">Review</a><a href="#state">Claim state</a><a href="#research">Research process</a><a href="#limits">Inference limits</a><a href="#publication">Publication</a><a href="#rights">Rights</a>
    </nav>

    <section id="evidence" class="panel">
      <h2>Three independent dimensions</h2>
      <p><strong>Provenance</strong> says where an assertion originated; <strong>review activity</strong> says what evidence was actually inspected or tested; <strong>claim state</strong> says how an assertion stands against the available evidence. Neither a prestigious publisher nor a reproduced behavior automatically makes a broader interpretation correct. A disputed statement can be well sourced; a vendor statement can be accurately attributed without being independently tested.</p>
      <p>Each claim also carries a <strong>kind</strong> (observation, inference, guidance or unknown), applicability, review date, limitations and citation locators. Scope applies to the claim, not every version of a system. A citation relation distinguishes support, contradiction and context; context alone does not corroborate. Source availability, retrieval transport and immutable revision identity are recorded separately.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="provenance" class="panel">
      <h2>Source provenance: who supplied the material?</h2>
      <div class="table-wrap"><table class="data-table">
        <thead><tr><th scope="col">Label</th><th scope="col">Meaning, not a guarantee</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><th scope="row">Vendor</th><td>Product developer or operator describes its own implementation, policy or response. Attribution is not independent efficacy testing.</td></tr>
          <tr><th scope="row">Publication</th><td>Published third-party reporting or technical analysis; its own methods and version scope still matter.</td></tr>
          <tr><th scope="row">Repository</th><td>Project code or documentation; a commit identifies a revision, not proof of what the code does in a deployed environment.</td></tr>
          <tr><th scope="row">Community</th><td>Public user or community report; useful as a lead, not independently corroborated by popularity.</td></tr>
          <tr><th scope="row">Academic</th><td>Scholarly research, subject to the paper's assumptions, experiments and publication date.</td></tr>
          <tr><th scope="row">Disclosure</th><td>Advisory or disclosed issue; affected versions, remediation and present-day exposure must be checked separately.</td></tr>
          <tr><th scope="row">Unverified</th><td>Origin or identity not sufficiently established; do not promote to a confirmed observation.</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table></div>
      <p>A source records publisher, access date, origin, publication date where known, revision (<span class="mono">git</span>, publication revision or explicitly unversioned), access (<span class="mono">available</span>, <span class="mono">blocked</span>, <span class="mono">not-retrieved</span>), transport (<span class="mono">direct</span>, <span class="mono">mirror</span>, <span class="mono">index-only</span>), rights and limitations. A mirror or index snippet does not silently become the original publication.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="review" class="panel">
      <h2>Review activity: what was done?</h2>
      <dl class="definitions">
        <div><dt>Collected</dt><dd>Identified and cataloged a source or claim; no source inspection or experiment is implied.</dd></div>
        <div><dt>Source-inspected</dt><dd>Read the cited source in its available form. This establishes what that source says, not independent truth or reproduction.</dd></div>
        <div><dt>Artifact-inspected</dt><dd>Inspected an identified artifact under the documented scope. A filename or source-reported hash alone is not artifact inspection.</dd></div>
        <div><dt>Behavior-reproduced</dt><dd>A bounded behavior was actually exercised with recorded environment, inputs, observed result, authority and limitations in a validation record. A source author's reported test and Observatory observation must remain distinct.</dd></div>
      </dl>
      <p>Validation records attribute who performed an activity, whether its result was merely reported or observed, and whether the outcome passed, failed or was inconclusive. Do not infer an Observatory reproduction from a third-party assertion or a project's README.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="state" class="panel">
      <h2>Claim state: what follows from the evidence?</h2>
      <dl class="definitions">
        <div><dt>Asserted</dt><dd>A statement is attributed, but not yet independently corroborated on its stated scope.</dd></div>
        <div><dt>Corroborated</dt><dd>Independent supporting material exists for the specific scoped assertion; this does not prove all versions or related assertions.</dd></div>
        <div><dt>Disputed</dt><dd>A substantive conflicting account remains unresolved. Keep both the challenge and supporting evidence visible.</dd></div>
        <div><dt>Refuted</dt><dd>The stated claim is contradicted by stronger scoped evidence; retain its history rather than silently deleting it.</dd></div>
        <div><dt>Superseded</dt><dd>A newer scoped claim replaces it; the older claim remains traceable and is not automatically false for its historical context.</dd></div>
      </dl>
      <p>Claims may link explicit contradictions, supersessions, corrections and validation records. A later repository commit, GitHub stars, source accessibility, or a period without enforcement cannot resolve a dispute on its own.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="research" class="panel">
      <h2>Research process</h2>
      <ol>
        <li><strong>Identify scope:</strong> product, component, environment, version/build where known, and the specific research question. A filename alone is not sample identity; a source-reported hash is not a project-computed hash.</li>
        <li><strong>Attribute:</strong> link each material claim to a global source, precise locator and its supporting, contradicting or contextual role. Record missing access and unversioned material honestly.</li>
        <li><strong>Separate:</strong> keep direct observations, inferences, guidance and unknowns distinct. Record prerequisites, limitations and counterevidence before drawing a conclusion.</li>
        <li><strong>Validate when possible:</strong> authorized reproduction requires a bounded environment, identifiable inputs and outputs, outcome and performer. Lack of reproduction stays visible.</li>
        <li><strong>Maintain:</strong> record corrections, disputes and newer evidence without rewriting a historical observation into a current deployment claim.</li>
      </ol>
      <p>Discovery items are leads from third-party metadata, not automatically reviewed claims. Retrieval failures do not erase previously collected data; upstream repository drift does not advance a reviewed commit or establish an implementation change.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="limits" class="panel">
      <h2>Inference limits</h2>
      <ul>
        <li>A legitimate vulnerable driver is not automatically malware; successful driver loading does not establish anti-cheat evasion.</li>
        <li>An import, filename or mention of a technique is not evidence of runtime behavior or a tested attack path.</li>
        <li>A past vulnerability does not establish current exposure; a vendor defense description does not establish comprehensive coverage.</li>
        <li>Absence of a ban does not demonstrate absence of detection; enforcement may be delayed.</li>
        <li>Kernel execution is not arbitrary control across all trust boundaries. Code virtualization and hypervisor virtualization are different topics.</li>
        <li>A missing dossier aspect or matrix mark means insufficient catalog coverage, never proof that a feature or boundary is absent.</li>
      </ul>
      <p><a href={withBase("/coverage")}>Inspect dossier gaps</a> · <a href={withBase("/matrix")}>Browse the trust boundary map</a></p>
    </section>

    <section id="publication" class="panel">
      <h2>Publication boundary</h2>
      <p>Publish architecture, root causes, scope, historical incidents, open questions and defensive lessons. Do not publish proprietary driver binaries, ready-to-run cheats, bypass payloads, secrets, private telemetry or personal information. Undisclosed vulnerabilities belong in the affected vendor's security reporting process before public discussion; no response is not evidence of a fix. Blocking a driver can disrupt legitimate devices and is not a universal defense.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="rights" class="panel">
      <h2>Provenance &amp; rights</h2>
      <p>Summaries and citation links do not grant permission to copy or redistribute third-party publications, software, screenshots or binaries. Source rights are recorded alongside access and transport; original publisher terms still apply. Vendor names and trademarks identify their owners; this independent project is not endorsed by the vendors or linked projects. Public access to the data export is not a blanket license over linked artifacts. Consult the repository's current license terms before redistributing project content.</p>
      <p>This project's application code is licensed under <a href="https://opensource.org/license/mit" rel="noopener noreferrer">MIT</a>; its original written content and catalog data are licensed under <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/" rel="noopener noreferrer">CC BY 4.0</a>. Repository files <code>LICENSE</code> and <code>LICENSE-CONTENT</code> define that separation. These grants do not relicense linked third-party works or attributed excerpts.</p>
      <p>The approach draws inspiration from <a href="https://lolbas-project.github.io/" rel="noopener noreferrer">LOLBAS</a>, <a href="https://www.loldrivers.io/" rel="noopener noreferrer">LOLDrivers</a> and <a href="https://malapi.io/" rel="noopener noreferrer">MalAPI</a>; none is an endorsement or evidence about a particular anti-cheat.</p>
      <a class="button" href={withBase("/data")}>Explore versioned data exports</a>
    </section>
  </div>
</Layout>

  .definitions { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 19rem), 1fr)); gap: .75rem 1.5rem; }
```

```astro
  <script>
    const search = document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>("#project-search")!;
    const platform = document.querySelector<HTMLSelectElement>("#project-platform")!;
    const state = document.querySelector<HTMLSelectElement>("#project-state")!;
    const rows = [...document.querySelectorAll<HTMLTableRowElement>("[data-project]")].map((element) => ({
      element,
      text: element.dataset.search ?? "",
      platforms: JSON.parse(element.dataset.platforms ?? "[]") as string[],
      state: element.dataset.state ?? "",
    }));
    const count = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#project-count")!;
    const reset = document.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>("#project-reset")!;
    const empty = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#project-empty")!;
    function update(writeUrl = true) {
      const tokens = search.value.normalize("NFKC").toLocaleLowerCase("en").trim().split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
      let visible = 0;
      for (const row of rows) {
        const matches = tokens.every((token) => row.text.includes(token)) &&
          (!platform.value || row.platforms.includes(platform.value)) &&
          (!state.value || row.state === state.value);
        row.element.hidden = !matches;
        if (matches) visible++;
      }
      count.textContent = `${visible} of ${rows.length} projects`;
      empty.hidden = visible !== 0;
      reset.hidden = !search.value && !platform.value && !state.value;
      if (writeUrl) {
        const query = new URLSearchParams();
        if (search.value.trim()) query.set("q", search.value.trim());
        if (platform.value) query.set("platform", platform.value);
        if (state.value) query.set("state", state.value);
        history.replaceState(null, "", `${location.pathname}${query.size ? `?${query}` : ""}${location.hash}`);
      }
    }
    function load() {
      const query = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
      search.value = query.get("q") ?? "";
      platform.value = query.get("platform") ?? "";
      state.value = query.get("state") ?? "";
      update(false);
    }
    for (const field of [search, platform, state]) field.addEventListener("input", () => update());
    reset.addEventListener("click", () => { search.value = ""; platform.value = ""; state.value = ""; update(); search.focus(); });
    window.addEventListener("popstate", load);
    load();
  </script>
</Layout>
```

`src/pages/records/[id].astro`:

```astro
---
import Layout from "../../layouts/Layout.astro";
import ClaimEvidence from "../../components/ClaimEvidence.astro";
import ProductMap from "../../components/ProductMap.astro";
import RepoPanel from "../../components/RepoPanel.astro";
import { records, recordById, kindNames, sectionId, projectsForProduct } from "../../lib/catalog";
import { postsForRecord } from "../../lib/research";
import {
  claimsForRecord, claimsByIds, sourcesByIds, sourcesForRecord, buildsForSystem,
  mechanismsForSystem, correctionsForRecord, dossierForSystem, systemsForRecord,
  relationshipsFor, buildById, mechanismById, sourceById, claimById,
} from "../../lib/knowledge";
import { dossierAspects, type CatalogRecord, type Claim, type BuildSample, type Mechanism } from "../../lib/knowledge-types";
import { editUrl, withBase } from "../../lib/paths";

export function getStaticPaths() {
  return records.map((record) => ({ params: { id: record.id }, props: { record } }));
}
interface Props { record: CatalogRecord }
const { record } = Astro.props;
const isProduct = record.kind === "product";
const scopedClaims = claimsForRecord(record.id);
const scopedIds = new Set(scopedClaims.map((claim) => claim.id));
const sections = record.sections.map((section, index) => ({
  title: section.title, id: sectionId(section.title, index),
  claims: claimsByIds(section.claimIds).filter((claim) => scopedIds.has(claim.id)),
}));
const sectionClaimIds = new Set(sections.flatMap((section) => section.claims.map((claim) => claim.id)));
const additionalClaims = scopedClaims.filter((claim) => !sectionClaimIds.has(claim.id));
const systems = systemsForRecord(record.id);
const builds = [...new Map<string, BuildSample>([
  ...record.buildIds.map((id) => buildById(id)).filter((build) => build != null),
  ...(isProduct ? buildsForSystem(record.id) : []),
].map((build) => [build.id, build] as const)).values()];
const mechanisms = isProduct ? mechanismsForSystem(record.id) : [];
const recordMechanisms = new Map<string, Mechanism>([
  ...mechanisms,
  ...record.mechanismIds.map((id) => mechanismById(id)).filter((mechanism) => mechanism != null),
].map((mechanism) => [mechanism.id, mechanism] as const));
const corrections = correctionsForRecord(record.id);
const dossier = isProduct ? dossierForSystem(record.id) : undefined;
const dossierRows = dossierAspects.map((id) => dossier?.aspects.find((aspect) => aspect.id === id) ??
  { id, status: "unknown" as const, claimIds: [], questions: [] });
const related = records.filter((entry) => entry.id !== record.id &&
  (record.relatedIds.includes(entry.id) || entry.relatedIds.includes(record.id)));
const reading = postsForRecord(record.id);
const projects = isProduct ? projectsForProduct(record.id) : [];
const sourceIds = new Set([
  ...sourcesForRecord(record.id).map((source) => source.id),
  ...scopedClaims.flatMap((claim) => claim.citations.map((citation) => citation.sourceId)),
  ...builds.flatMap((build) => build.sourceIds),
  ...corrections.flatMap((correction) => correction.sourceIds),
]);
const sources = sourcesByIds([...sourceIds]);
const relationships = relationshipsFor(record.id);
const claimHref = (claimId: string) => scopedIds.has(claimId) ? `#claim-${claimId}` : withBase(`/claims/${claimId}`);
const evidenceHref = (id: string) => sourceById(id) ? withBase(`/sources/${id}`) : claimById(id) ? claimHref(id) : undefined;
const entityHref = (id: string) => recordById(id) ? withBase(`/records/${id}`) : mechanismById(id) ? withBase(`/mechanisms/${id}`) : buildById(id) ? withBase(`/builds/${id}`) : sourceById(id) ? withBase(`/sources/${id}`) : claimById(id) ? withBase(`/claims/${id}`) : undefined;
const entityTitle = (id: string) => recordById(id)?.title ?? mechanismById(id)?.title ?? buildById(id)?.label ?? sourceById(id)?.title ?? claimById(id)?.statement ?? id;
const edit = editUrl(`src/data/records/${record.id}.json`);
---

        </section>
        <section id="record-components" class="record-section">

          {isProduct ? <ProductMap product={record} /> : <p class="muted">{record.kind === "component" ? "This component's documented scope and filenames appear above; linked catalog records appear in the outline." : "Related components and systems, where documented, are linked in the outline."}</p>}

        <section id="record-mechanisms" class="record-section">
```
